why.founding: An Imperial signal tower on the rim, built to talk to Fort Swampmoth by fire and kept lit by the people who now hold neither.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge end with a line to the fort and a line down the road — the only point that has both.
why.occupantsMotive: The two watchers are paid in food by four villages who want warning of raids, not of armies.
why.pressures: The fire code they use was written for legions and now means things it did not mean.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the day the villages decided the Sul-Xan were finished.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands a route or a channel
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower

vibe.silhouette: A round stone stump three storeys high with an iron basket on top, ash spilling down one side.
vibe.palette: Ash grey on grey stone, rust, and at night an orange point.
vibe.materials: Imperial rubble tower, timber floors renewed in local wood, an iron basket nobody could make today.
vibe.signatureFeature: The code board inside: the Legion's fire signals, annotated in Jel down the margin.
vibe.condition: The lower two storeys are sound; the top floor is new timber on old corbels.
vibe.approach: The ash streak down the stonework is visible before the tower reads as a tower.
vibe.senses: Wind through arrow slits; the basket ticking as it cools.

places.name: Bog Iron Workings

why.founding: Bog iron forms itself in this ground, and a road that eats iron will pay for it.
why.siteAdvantages: A stagnant iron-rich seep where the ore can be lifted from the mud in cakes.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers are seasonal, come from three villages, and consider the work slightly shameful.
why.pressures: The seep is being worked out; each season's cakes are smaller and further from the path.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned without ceremony, and the province would think better of itself for it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a road or a foreign settlement
preferences: a drying rack for peat fuel

occupants: D3 something in the deeper pools

vibe.silhouette: Orange water, black spoil, a clay bloomery mound like a termite hill, and boot-boards laid over mud.
vibe.palette: Rust orange, peat black, sick yellow scum.
vibe.materials: Clay furnace, timber boards, reed baskets — nothing permanent, nothing beautiful.
vibe.signatureFeature: The orange water: the seep stains everything it touches, including the workers, to the knee.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt every season because the mound is broken open to get the bloom out.
vibe.approach: The water colour is visible through the reeds well before the workings are.
vibe.senses: Sucking mud; a hollow ring when a bloom is struck; sulphur.

places.name: Bonded Shed

why.founding: Goods that have been declared but not yet taxed have to sit somewhere lockable, and Gideon's court is the only body that can hold them lawfully.
why.siteAdvantages: On the river landing directly below the city, so a cart can be sealed at the wharf and opened in court.
why.occupantsMotive: The bond-keeper's authority comes from the courthouse and nowhere else, which he mentions often.
why.pressures: Half the bond is Cyrodilic Collections crates and half is what the antiquities fences shipped instead; the labels do not always match.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be looted in a night if the courthouse ever stopped sitting.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: attached to a port or a wharf
preferences: a court seal on the door

occupants: one D3 investigator when a seal is broken

vibe.silhouette: A long windowless shed on stone piers with one door and a great many seals on it.
vibe.palette: Tar black boards, wax red seals, river silver.
vibe.materials: Imperial timber frame on stone piers, reed above the tie beam because the roof was rebuilt locally.
vibe.signatureFeature: The seal course: every seal ever applied, left in place, so the door is scaled with wax.
vibe.condition: Sound and deliberately unlovely.
vibe.approach: You come at it along the wharf; it is the only building on the river with no windows.
vibe.senses: Wax; river damp; a padlock the size of a fist.

places.name: Carries-Them-Home
sources: uesp:Lore:Argonian (bones brought to the dirt redeem a death away from the Hist)

why.founding: Bones travelling home need stages, and the western route is the longest carry in the province.
why.siteAdvantages: A day's carry from the counted dead and a day from the marsh edge — the spacing is the institution.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers house carriers and take custody of bones overnight, which is an office of enormous trust.
why.pressures: More bones come west than go east, and the imbalance is a political fact everyone notices.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be busier than the road itself if the Chainbreakers ever emptied White Rose.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a walked or poled route
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: between a carceral site and the interior
hardConstraints: one day's carry from the next stage
preferences: a bone house separate from the sleeping house

vibe.silhouette: Two houses forty paces apart: one with a hearth and one with no hearth at all.
vibe.palette: Thatch gold, whitewash, and the bone house painted with white clay to the eaves.
vibe.materials: Mud and reed; the bone house is limewashed and everything else is not.
vibe.signatureFeature: The separation: the deliberate empty ground between the living house and the bone house.
vibe.condition: Kept beautifully; the limewash is renewed monthly.
vibe.approach: Two roofs with a gap, on an open path — the gap is the thing you notice.
vibe.senses: Wind between the two houses; low talk; no music.

places.name: Burnt Field
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (Legate Elissia Mallicius set the marsh alight, 1E 2828)

why.founding: A village that returned to ground the Legion burned, because it was theirs and because the peat still smoulders and the smoulder keeps outsiders off.
why.siteAdvantages: The one patch inside the burn where the peat burned out completely and left mineral soil.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay to hold the claim; the smoke is a defence they did not have to build.
why.pressures: Sinkholes open without warning where the peat has burned out below; two houses have gone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate the day the underground fire reached their side of the scar — and it is moving.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the burn country of the west

notableNpcSlots: the fire-watcher who maps the smoulder

vibe.silhouette: Pale new houses on black ground, with thin smoke coming out of the earth behind them in three places.
vibe.palette: Charcoal black, ash white, the sharp green of first-year regrowth.
vibe.materials: Mud and reed, all of it new, none of it built on anything.
vibe.signatureFeature: The smoulder map scratched on the fire-watcher's door: where the ground is hot this year.
vibe.condition: Everything is under nine years old, because everything before that burned.
vibe.approach: The colour changes under your feet a kilometre out and the smell arrives before the roofs.
vibe.senses: Peat smoke; ground that sounds hollow; almost no insects.

places.name: Cartwright's Cross

why.founding: A town grew where the Blackwood Road crosses the north track, because a crossroads is a place where money must stop.
why.siteAdvantages: Level firm ground with a spring, at the one crossing that cannot be bypassed without a day's detour.
why.occupantsMotive: Four families hold the four corners and split the crossing dues, an arrangement older than the courthouse.
why.pressures: Gideon claims the dues are unlawful and collects a tax on the town instead, which everyone finds cheaper than arguing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would decline sharply if the north track were ever bridged upstream.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a road or boat lane; day-travel spacing from the next
hardConstraints: a road crossing that cannot be bypassed

notableNpcSlots: the four corner-holders, who agree on nothing

vibe.silhouette: Four two-storey corner houses facing each other across a crossroads, with the town filling in behind them.
vibe.palette: Cart-grease black, ochre plaster, the four corner-houses each painted a different colour.
vibe.materials: Mud-brick and timber, Imperial road stone underfoot, one tiled roof per corner as a boast.
vibe.signatureFeature: The four colours: each corner family's paint, renewed annually, competitively.
vibe.condition: Busy, cluttered, repaired with whatever the last cart was carrying.
vibe.approach: Both roads run at it dead straight; you can see the crossing from either arm.
vibe.senses: Iron tyres on stone; hammering; four different bells.

places.name: Cassian's Holding

why.founding: A Nibenese family took a land grant here five generations ago and, unusually, made it work.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry loam shoulder above the flood line, with the river close enough to lift water and far enough not to take the barn.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because the land is theirs on paper and, by now, in fact; the neighbours accept them and mock the paper.
why.pressures: The grant describes fields that are now river, and the family will not admit it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end in a generation if the heir marries out, which she intends to.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: tried to be dry and failed
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing

notableNpcSlots: the heir who intends to marry out

vibe.silhouette: A tiled farmhouse with a walled yard and a barn up on mushroom stones, in fields that are too rectangular for this province.
vibe.palette: Terracotta, whitewash, and crop green in straight lines.
vibe.materials: Imperial farmhouse stone and pantile; the field hands' quarters are reed and mud fifty metres away.
vibe.signatureFeature: The staddle-stone barn, standing clear of the ground on stone mushrooms so nothing can climb in.
vibe.condition: Prosperous and slightly over-repaired, the way a family that fears looking poor repairs things.
vibe.approach: The straight field edges announce it from further than the roof does.
vibe.senses: Hens; a dog chain; somebody counting in Cyrodiilic.

places.name: Castle Giovesse

why.founding: A Cyrodiilic ducal seat raised in arm's reach of Gideon's north gate, later used to hold an Empress.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry knoll above the flood line with a clear line to the city gate — the site was chosen to be looked at.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the caretaker families who once did left when the well went bad, and the city tells its children not to go.
why.pressures: Roots in the vaulting; the north range has already gone; treasure-hunters chip at the cell doors.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be reoccupied the moment anyone in Gideon wanted a stone house badly enough — which, post-Duskfall, nobody does.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: dominating ground nobody else wanted
hardConstraints: within sight of Gideon's north gate
preferences: a ruined curtain with one standing tower

occupants: D3 restless dead in the cell range
notableNpcSlots: the ghost the city calls Tavia, whether or not she is

vibe.silhouette: A broken square keep with one intact stair turret, black against the evening from the city wall.
vibe.palette: Bone-grey stone, black damp streaks, the violent green of fig roots.
vibe.materials: Imperial ashlar and vault ribs, no timber left at all.
vibe.signatureFeature: Empress Tavia's cell, still identifiable, its door hinges still in the jamb.
vibe.condition: Roofless, root-split, structurally treacherous above the first floor.
vibe.mood: Aggrieved and domestic — a house that was made into a prison and never forgave it.
vibe.approach: A track through fig scrub, then the ditch, then the gate arch with the ducal arms hacked flat.
vibe.senses: Wind in an empty stair; bats; the smell of wet stone dust.

provisions: haunted ruin in arm's reach of a city

places.name: Claywater Station

why.founding: A mixed village at the road's water point, where the Imperial well and the Argonian landing serve the same travellers.
why.siteAdvantages: A perennial spring beside a boat channel — the one place the road and the water actually touch on level terms.
why.occupantsMotive: Two communities share it because neither can hold the other's half.
why.pressures: The well is Imperial-built and failing, and repairing it in stone is a thing the Argonian half will not help with.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become one community or two villages within a generation; nobody knows which.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing along a road
hardConstraints: a perennial spring on the road

notableNpcSlots: the well-keeper
the landing's poler

vibe.silhouette: A stone well head with a tiled roof on one side of the road; reed houses on stilts over water on the other.
vibe.palette: Wet stone grey against reed gold; the two halves do not share a colour.
vibe.materials: Imperial well masonry and pantile; Argonian stilt frames and reed — adjacent, unblended, per the two-culture kit rule.
vibe.signatureFeature: The road as the boundary: it is a village made of two villages facing each other.
vibe.condition: The stone half is cracking; the reed half was rebuilt last year.
vibe.approach: The well roof shows first; then you realise the other side of the road is on stilts.
vibe.senses: A windlass; water poured; two languages across one street.

places.name: Licensed Dig

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections refounded at Gideon and immediately needed something to dig, so it licensed the nearest Ayleid ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly below Twyllbek's terrace, on flat ground with cart access to the city.
why.occupantsMotive: The Collections dig to return things; the local hands dig for wages; the fences watch to see what is found.
why.pressures: The permit is Gideon's, the ground is nobody's, and the tribes who might object have not been asked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be shut down in a day if the council ever decided the fences paid better.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always beside a ruin

notableNpcSlots: the chapter-agent who signs the finds out
the local foreman who signs nothing

vibe.silhouette: A white conservation tent, a pegged grid of trenches, and a spoil heap sorted into four sizes.
vibe.palette: Canvas white, spoil brown, string-line yellow.
vibe.materials: Canvas, rope, timber shoring — an entirely temporary camp with a permanent-looking system.
vibe.signatureFeature: The find table under the tent, where every object is drawn before it is moved.
vibe.condition: Neat, disciplined, expensively supplied.
vibe.approach: The tent is the only white surface in the landscape and it glows at dusk.
vibe.senses: Trowels; a hand bell for finds; a generator of argument in three languages.

provisions: a foreign presence to argue with

places.name: Fenmarch

why.founding: The westernmost Hist stands here, and a village stands where a Hist stands.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm hummock at the marsh's western limit, with the tree already ancient when the village came.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because the tree is here; the tree's westernmost position makes them the province's edge in the way that matters.
why.pressures: Gideon's disputed cutting came from this tree, and Fenmarch's opinion of that is unprintable.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not move. A Hist village is the one Argonian settlement that does not relocate.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one to two hours from its neighbours by water; clusters along a drainage
preferences: houses in a ring at root distance

occupants: one strong D3 who speaks for the tree
notableNpcSlots: the naheesh
the tree-minder who opposed the cutting

vibe.silhouette: A single vast pale-barked crown standing well above the marsh canopy, with roofs in a ring beneath it.
vibe.palette: Hist bark grey-white, canopy green, thatch gold, and the amber of the uxith lamps at night.
vibe.materials: Mud and reed houses, an uxith of grown rather than built material, and the tree, which is not architecture.
vibe.signatureFeature: The root ring: houses set exactly at the distance the roots permit, so the village plan is drawn by the tree.
vibe.condition: Constantly rebuilt at the edges, unchanged at the centre.
vibe.mood: Rooted, self-possessed, faintly cold towards Gideon.
vibe.approach: The crown breaks the canopy — the west's second true landmark, and the only living one.
vibe.senses: Wind in a crown far above; the uxith; frogs; a village that goes quiet at root talk.

places.name: Fig Market

why.founding: The marsh's produce and the road's manufactures have to change hands somewhere neither side controls.
why.siteAdvantages: A landing on the last navigable reach with cart ground behind it — boat and cart meet at the same quay.
why.occupantsMotive: The town lives on the spread between the two, and its guild of brokers exists to keep the spread.
why.pressures: Gideon wants the market inside its walls and has tried twice; the brokers pay it not to try a third time.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into a village if the navigable reach silted a kilometre downstream.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the hinge of a district; several villages depend on it
hardConstraints: boat and cart access to one quay

notableNpcSlots: the broker who fixes the spread
the boat-mistress who knows the reach

vibe.silhouette: A long covered market shed with a quay at one end and fig trees down the middle of the street.
vibe.palette: Fig-leaf green, sun-bleached awning, river brown, and the market shed's black tar roof.
vibe.materials: Argonian reed and mud on stilted platforms by the water, mud-brick shops uphill, one tar-roofed communal shed.
vibe.signatureFeature: The spread board: today's buying and selling prices, side by side, publicly and shamelessly.
vibe.condition: Crowded, extended sideways every few years, structurally chaotic.
vibe.approach: The tar roof is the biggest single surface for a kilometre and shows over the trees from the water.
vibe.senses: Haggling; boats knocking the quay; overripe figs.

places.name: Fort Greenditch

why.founding: The second of the road forts, built to hold the marsh side of the frontier and emptied with the rest at the Oblivion Crisis.
why.siteAdvantages: A low spur over the marsh edge; good against an army, useless against water, which is what actually came.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody holds it: the ditch flooded, the ground floor with it, and the toll company judged it not worth the pumping.
why.pressures: Something has been using the gatehouse, and the villages have stopped cutting reed on that side.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be as valuable as Swampmoth if the ditch were ever drained — which is a two-season job and a quest.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands something that no longer matters
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a dead road

occupants: D3 whatever is in the gatehouse

vibe.silhouette: A square fort standing in its own moat, reflected perfectly, with reeds growing inside the walls.
vibe.palette: Green ditch water, grey wall, reed gold inside the courtyard.
vibe.materials: Imperial fort masonry; the timber floors are gone and the reeds have colonised the parade.
vibe.signatureFeature: The reflection: from the causeway the fort and its double are the same size, which reads as a landmark and a warning.
vibe.condition: Walls sound, everything internal drowned or rotted.
vibe.mood: Still, green, wrong in a way that takes a moment.
vibe.approach: The wall shows over the reeds from a long way, and then the water in front of it does.
vibe.senses: Frogs inside the walls; wind through empty embrasures; a splash you did not make.

places.name: Fort Swampmoth

why.founding: Built by the Third Empire to hold the only land approach into the province; rumoured emptied when the Legions were recalled at the Oblivion Crisis.
why.siteAdvantages: Commands the Blackwood Road where it leaves the ridge for the flood plain — nothing wheeled passes without being seen.
why.occupantsMotive: The outfit that moved in two centuries ago charges for passage and calls it upkeep; it has a written claim and will show it to you.
why.pressures: Gideon's council would rather the tolls were theirs; the Marsh Charter's people regard a foreign fort held by toll-takers as an insult with a gate.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change hands entirely if the road moved, or if the council ever paid to garrison it properly.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands a road or a crossing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a road between the border and a city
preferences: a ridge nose with a long view down the road

occupants: a clerk who is not a soldier
notableNpcSlots: the captain with the claim
the clerk who forges the receipts

vibe.silhouette: A square Imperial keep and curtain wall on a ridge nose, moss to the string course, banners that are not Imperial banners.
vibe.palette: Grey basalt-grey stone, rust, red road clay, the green rising up the north face.
vibe.materials: Imperial fort masonry, timber hoardings added since, a wattle stock pen where the parade ground was.
vibe.signatureFeature: The Imperial eagle still over the gate because nobody bothered to chisel it off.
vibe.condition: Structurally sound, socially illegitimate; repaired in wood by people with no masons.
vibe.mood: Officious, mercenary, faintly embarrassed — men playing at being a garrison.
vibe.approach: The road bends and the wall is simply there, higher than anything you have seen since Leyawiin.
vibe.senses: Chain and windlass; the toll bell; goats in the ditch.

provisions: Fort Swampmoth, held but not by the Empire

places.name: Gideon

why.founding: Founded where the Blackwood Road out of Leyawiin crosses the one low saddle in the western border belt — the province's only land door.
why.siteAdvantages: A measured 46 m barrier gap flanked by 60–87 m ridges; firm lowland and drinkable spring water on the marsh side; the Onkobra's red clay downstream.
why.occupantsMotive: A civic council in the old Governor's Mansion keeps the courthouse and archive working because paper is the only authority anyone here still recognises, and because Leyawiin trade pays for it.
why.pressures: Monsoon closes the road for months; the archive's writs are honoured nowhere east of the Onkobra; Cyrodilic Collections and the antiquities fences fight over the same crates.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fail if the Blackwood Road silted permanently, or if the disputed Hist cutting in the city gardens took root and made Gideon an Argonian city rather than a filing cabinet.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: river port on a road river
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the western terminus of every road in the province; Leyawiin two days out
hardConstraints: river landing for the Onkobra trade
preferences: ground for a walled records quarter
gardens for the disputed Hist cutting

occupants: ordinary D1 townsfolk (Argonian majority, large Imperial minority)
notableNpcSlots: the sitting magistrate
the Collections chapter-agent
the gardens' Hist-minder
the wintertide rootworm waykeeper

vibe.silhouette: Low tiled roofs and a squat courthouse tower stepping up a saddle, with one impossible green crown in the gardens behind it.
vibe.palette: Fired red clay, wet slate, Nibenese ochre, and the marsh's grey-green pressing in at the gate.
vibe.materials: Cyrodiilic dressed stone and timber below the eaves, red pantile, Argonian reed and mud in every quarter the council does not photograph.
vibe.signatureFeature: The Records Court: a stone archive whose ground floor floods every monsoon, so the province's history is stored on the first floor and up a ladder.
vibe.condition: Maintained but patched with local materials — imperial masonry with wattle repairs, which nobody finds funny any more.
vibe.mood: Bureaucratic, dry-witted, quietly humiliated; the last office in Argonia that still stamps things.
vibe.approach: From the west the road climbs out of the Blackwood trees and the town simply appears in the notch, roofs first; from the east it is a wall of pale stone at the end of the marsh.
vibe.senses: Wet paper and clay dust; the courthouse bell; guar carts; frogs from the gardens pond at dusk.

provisions: Cyrodilic Collections refounded at Gideon (unbuilt-museum-site district)

places.complexityJustification: A major city: districts, a walled records core, a foreign quarter and a seasonal root terminus. Placement complexity stays Morrowind-level — kit assemblies on a graded saddle — but the district count justifies the budget.

heroHist.note: Hero Hist 4/10. EXTRAPOLATED (hist-placement.md §3): a cutting planted in the city gardens among the Ayleid ruins — speaking, but young by Hist standards and of disputed provenance, with a Gloommire tribe claiming it was taken. Canon permits transplanting (the Blackwood Company's smuggled tree) and the quest plan's MR03 assumes exactly this. Gideon is also the western terminus of the rootworm line.

places.name: Wintertide Stop

why.founding: The rootworms migrate south to Gideon in wintertide and not otherwise; the stop exists only while they are here.
why.siteAdvantages: A root-layer breach in the clay bank outside the city where the worms surface — marked by red clay because red clay is what is to hand.
why.occupantsMotive: The waykeepers keep the marks and the etiquette; Gideon's carters keep the freight rates.
why.pressures: It is a season, not a service: the quest plan forbids any year-round Gideon root transit, and Gideon's council keeps trying to make it one.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end for good if the potters cut the bank back past the breach.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: nodes on the root network; not on any map

occupants: nothing at all out of season
notableNpcSlots: the wintertide waykeeper

vibe.silhouette: Out of season: a red-daubed post in a clay bank and a flattened waiting circle. In season: a mound of moving earth.
vibe.palette: Wet red clay, worm-translucent pink, wintertide grey sky.
vibe.materials: Daubed marks, mats, a rope rail — nothing that could not be abandoned in an hour.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tally post, red-daubed once per arrival for as long as anyone has counted.
vibe.condition: Unbuilt on purpose.
vibe.mood: Expectant in wintertide; a bare field the rest of the year, and the bareness is the point.
vibe.approach: You follow red daub marks on trees away from the road until they stop at a bank.
vibe.senses: In season: the ground itself moving, and a smell like turned compost.

provisions: wintertide rootworm migration stop, seasonal only

places.name: Reckoning House

why.founding: The Synod inherited the Mages Guild's ambitions and sent an outstation to the one city with an archive it could read.
why.siteAdvantages: Inside Gideon's reach but outside its walls, on ground the council leased cheaply to keep them at arm's length.
why.occupantsMotive: They are here to inventory and, quietly, to acquire; the province is a collection to them.
why.pressures: The Whispers house across the marsh is here for the same reason and they do not speak.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be recalled the moment Cyrodiil decided the province was not worth the stipend.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in or near a northern city; rival to the Whispers
hardConstraints: within a day of a functioning archive

notableNpcSlots: the magister who wants the courthouse archive

vibe.silhouette: A compact stone house with a flat leaded roof and instruments on it, all straight lines and shut windows.
vibe.palette: Cold grey stone, lead, brass, one blue-lit window at night.
vibe.materials: Imported dressed stone — an offence here, and they do not know it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The roof instruments, turned to the sky in a province where the sky is usually invisible.
vibe.condition: New, exact, already streaked green with damp they did not anticipate.
vibe.mood: Officious, foreign, faintly ridiculous, genuinely dangerous.
vibe.approach: The flat roofline is wrong against every other roof for a kilometre; that is how you find it.
vibe.senses: A humming ward; brass on stone; no local voices.

places.name: Glenbridge

why.founding: Pilgrims from all over Tamriel come to hear the Nisswo read a ruined Sithis xanmeer's decay as the god's sermon; a town grew to feed them.
why.siteAdvantages: A bridged glen on the last easy ground before the bog — the only place the pilgrim road can cross and the only place it can stop.
why.occupantsMotive: The Nisswo stay because the sermon is not finished until the stone is gone; the innkeepers stay because pilgrims eat.
why.pressures: Foreign pilgrims want the ruin preserved; the Nisswo find that blasphemous. Rectavius is still sealed below and the seal is two centuries older than anyone tending it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a season if the xanmeer finally collapsed — which is, theologically, the point.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with a hero Hist, a Sithis temple or a trial ground
hardConstraints: within sight of the sermon xanmeer
preferences: a market square that can hold a crowd

notableNpcSlots: the reading Nisswo
the innkeeper who keeps the wager book on which stone falls next

vibe.silhouette: A single stone-arched bridge, a market square, and a half-eaten pyramid on the skyline above the roofs.
vibe.palette: Warm ochre thatch, pale ruin stone, black Nisswo cloth.
vibe.materials: Local mud-and-wattle houses, one honest Imperial-built bridge, and stone only where the dead built it.
vibe.signatureFeature: The wager board in the square: which block falls next, and by when.
vibe.condition: Prosperous, well-swept, entirely dependent on a building falling down.
vibe.mood: Devout, cheerful, morbid in a way visitors take a day to notice.
vibe.approach: The road drops into the glen; you hear the market before you see the ruin above it.
vibe.senses: Chanting on the hour; hammers on nothing; hot oil and river weed.

provisions: village around the ruined Sithis xanmeer

places.name: Sermon Xanmeer

why.founding: A Merethic Sithis temple deliberately left to decay so that its decay could be read aloud as scripture.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands above Glenbridge on the glen's shoulder, so the whole town can watch the sermon progress.
why.occupantsMotive: The Nisswo read it; the Clutch below them sweeps nothing away, because sweeping would be a lie.
why.pressures: The voriplasm-sorcerer Rectavius is sealed in the lowest chamber, and the seal is part of the structure that is being allowed to fail.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become the province's worst problem the day the sermon reaches the bottom course.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a regional pilgrimage terminus
hardConstraints: above Glenbridge, visible from its square

occupants: D3 voriplasm seepage below the third course
notableNpcSlots: the sealer's heir, who has never opened the door

vibe.silhouette: A stepped pyramid missing its top three courses, a black doorway at the base like a bite.
vibe.palette: Grey-white stone stained with green runnels; black cloth on the reading stand.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer tileset ashlar; nothing has been added and nothing repaired.
vibe.signatureFeature: The reading stand on the second terrace, worn by three centuries of elbows.
vibe.condition: Failing on purpose; every fallen block left exactly where it landed and numbered.
vibe.approach: You climb from the market past numbered rubble; the numbers get lower as you get higher.
vibe.senses: Grit falling; the reader's voice; a wet chemical smell from the doorway.

places.name: Nine Bells Guar Holding

why.founding: The Blackwood Road runs on guar, and guar have to be bred, broken and rested somewhere within a day of the city.
why.siteAdvantages: Rough grazing too poor for crops and too dry for rice, which is exactly what a guar herd wants.
why.occupantsMotive: The holding sells draught animals to carters and hires out handlers, and its hands are the best-paid labour in the zone.
why.pressures: Rootworm season unsettles the herd badly, and wintertide is the holding's worst month.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would double in size if the road ever ran year-round.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: tried to be dry and failed
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing

notableNpcSlots: the breaker who names every animal

vibe.silhouette: Rail pens on open grazing, a bell on each of nine gates, one round sand ring.
vibe.palette: Dust, hide-grey and hide-green, weathered rail timber.
vibe.materials: Split-rail fence and a stone-footed byre; no walls the animals could not see over.
vibe.signatureFeature: The nine bells, each a different note, so the handlers know which gate opened without looking.
vibe.condition: Hard-worn, constantly mended, clean where it matters.
vibe.approach: You hear the bells long before you see a fence — the zone's audible cue.
vibe.senses: Guar calling; bells; hide and dung and dry grass.

places.name: Hearth House of the Burnt Field
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (Legate Mallicius set the marsh alight, 1E 2828)

why.founding: A hearth house raised on the edge of the old burn country because that is where people arrive exhausted.
why.siteAdvantages: The first ground with living trees on the eastern approach out of the burn.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by the burn-scar village downslope as a matter of pride: they of all people know what arriving hungry means.
why.pressures: The burn ground still supports almost nothing, so stocking it costs the village more than it can spare.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be moved further into the burn if anyone ever re-greened it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities
hardConstraints: at the edge of the burn ground

vibe.silhouette: A low house under the first three living trees, with the black ground starting fifty metres behind it.
vibe.palette: Charcoal black behind, green ahead, thatch gold between.
vibe.materials: Mud, wattle, thatch — and a hearth ring built from fire-cracked stone salvaged from the burn.
vibe.signatureFeature: The salvaged hearth: stones that were burnt in 1E 2828 and are being used to make fire again.
vibe.condition: Kept up at real cost; the thatch is thinner than it should be.
vibe.mood: Relieved. It is the place where the bad ground stops.
vibe.approach: Walking out of the burn, the trees begin and the roof is under them.
vibe.senses: Leaves — startling, after silence; water; wood being split.

why.founding: A dry rise in the flood plain will always be built on, because for four months a year it is the only ground there is.
why.siteAdvantages: A flood-high knoll that has never gone under in recorded memory, with landing on three sides in the wet.
why.occupantsMotive: The households here are the flood plain's landlords in the wet season and its equals in the dry.
why.pressures: The rise is small; there is no room to grow, and the third generation is having to leave.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned within a year of a flood that topped it, and the plain would lose its refuge.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: refuge for its neighbours in flood
hardConstraints: a rise that has never flooded

vibe.silhouette: Eight houses crowded onto a knoll that is a green island for a third of the year and a hill for the rest.
vibe.palette: Thatch gold on green in the dry; thatch gold on brown water in the wet.
vibe.materials: Mud, wattle and reed, packed so tightly the eaves touch — the only crowded village in the zone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The flood posts on the slope, marking each year's high water in a downward-drifting series.
vibe.condition: Dense, well kept, physically unable to expand.
vibe.mood: Snug, slightly claustrophobic, hospitable under pressure.
vibe.approach: In the wet season it is a village floating on a plain of water and reads from a kilometre.
vibe.senses: Everything at close quarters; water lapping at the fourth post; a great many frogs.

places.name: Hollow Arch

why.founding: The Onkobra's narrowest reach near the city was bridged in stone, and whoever holds a bridge in this province holds an income.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock nose on each bank: the only place a stone arch could land without piling.
why.occupantsMotive: Gideon's council farms the toll out annually to the highest bidder, which keeps the rate moving and the bidders unpopular.
why.pressures: The arch is hollow — a repair void the last farmer never filled — and the current one knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bypassed by the ford upstream if the toll ever rose above the price of wet feet.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: spans a channel at its narrowest
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight
preferences: a toll house on the city side

occupants: a Reed writ-reader on quarter days

vibe.silhouette: One high stone arch over green water with a toll house built into the parapet.
vibe.palette: Wet grey stone, black water, the toll board's flaking white.
vibe.materials: Imperial voussoirs and a bridge house of the same stone with a reed roof.
vibe.signatureFeature: The rate board, rewritten every year in a different hand and never fully erased.
vibe.condition: Sound above, visibly failing at the springing on the east side.
vibe.approach: The road runs at it straight; the toll house is under the parapet so you see the board before the man.
vibe.senses: Water under stone; coins; a chain across the deck at night.

places.name: Keeps-The-Lower-Water

why.founding: Gideon's hunting trade needs someone living on the ground it hunts, to say what may be taken and when.
why.siteAdvantages: On the river below the last village, where every boat going upstream must pass the door.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper licenses hunters and takes a share; the villages accept it because he also culls what kills their stock.
why.pressures: The poachers work around him, and he knows exactly who they are.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced by a village office if the Gideon trade ever collapsed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with a crossing, landing or light
hardConstraints: on the river at a choke point

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who knows the poachers' names

vibe.silhouette: A timber lodge on piles over the river bank with skulls fixed along the eaves, one per year.
vibe.palette: Bone white on dark timber, river brown, dog-yard dust.
vibe.materials: Stilted timber and reed; the only ornament is skeletal.
vibe.signatureFeature: The eaves line: one culled predator's skull per year, running the length of the building, oldest at the far end.
vibe.condition: Well kept, heavily used, smells of dogs.
vibe.approach: The skull line reads from the water at fifty metres and is meant to.
vibe.senses: Dogs; the river; a hide being scraped.

places.name: Long Causeway

why.founding: The village answer to the Imperial embankment: a floating timber causeway that rides the flood instead of blocking it.
why.siteAdvantages: Crosses the widest shallow between the Gideon hinterland and the marsh edge, where nothing can be piled.
why.occupantsMotive: Six villages own segments and each maintains its own, so the causeway's quality changes every two hundred metres.
why.pressures: One village's segment is always in dispute and therefore always the worst.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced piecemeal forever — that is how it works.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: links two named places directly

occupants: D2 in the water beneath at night

vibe.silhouette: A dark ribbon a hand's breadth above the water, running until it disappears into haze.
vibe.palette: Black wet timber, silver water, six subtly different timber colours where the segments meet.
vibe.materials: Buoyant lashed logs, reed matting, hand ropes on the disputed segment only.
vibe.signatureFeature: The segment marks: each village's totem set at its own boundary, six distinct carvings.
vibe.condition: Excellent, adequate, and one stretch that is frankly dangerous.
vibe.approach: It goes flat to the horizon; you cannot see the end from either end, which is the whole experience.
vibe.senses: Timber flexing underfoot; water inches away; a bird colony half a kilometre off.

places.name: Low-Water Fair

why.founding: When the water drops, a river bed becomes the widest flat surface in the marsh, and the villages that can only meet by boat can meet on foot.
why.siteAdvantages: A braided reach that dries to firm sand for eight weeks a year and is four metres deep the rest.
why.occupantsMotive: Villages come to settle marriages, debts and boundaries as much as to trade.
why.pressures: Anyone who miscalculates the rise loses their goods, and someone does most years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not exist at all in a wet year — and there have been three.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a landing, because most goods come by water
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement
preferences: boat moorings on both banks for the wet season

occupants: D2 river predators when the water returns

vibe.silhouette: A dry river bed floored with pale sand, mats laid straight on it, water still running in one thread down the middle.
vibe.palette: Bleached sand, wet-green banks, dyed mats in every colour the villages have.
vibe.materials: Mats, poles and tethered boats hauled up the bank; no structure touches the bed.
vibe.signatureFeature: The rise mark: a stake driven at the level the water reached last year, standing absurdly high above the fair.
vibe.condition: Immaculately temporary.
vibe.mood: Festive with an edge of hurry.
vibe.approach: You come down the bank and the fair is below the landscape, which no other market here is.
vibe.senses: Feet on sand; the single water thread; drums at dusk.

why.founding: Rice is the one crop that works in a province that floods, and Gideon eats.
why.siteAdvantages: A terraced flood plain with controllable inflow — the flood is the irrigation, if you own the sluice.
why.occupantsMotive: The families here own the water rather than the land, which is the local form of property.
why.pressures: The sluice was Imperial-built and one gate has jammed open since the Oblivion Crisis; the lower terraces are permanently wet.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worth twice as much with a working gate, which is a repair, not a revolution.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a city's hinterland; owned

vibe.silhouette: Stepped water mirrors down a shallow slope, each a slightly different green, with one stone sluice at the head.
vibe.palette: Twelve greens and a great deal of sky, reflected.
vibe.materials: Earth bunds, reed drying platforms, one Imperial stone sluice with an iron rack.
vibe.signatureFeature: The jammed gate, propped and silted, with a shrine's worth of offerings on it.
vibe.condition: Beautifully maintained in earth; irreparable in stone.
vibe.approach: You come over a low rise and the whole staircase of water is below you, flashing.
vibe.senses: Water stepping down; bird-scarers; frogs at an enormous volume after dark.

places.name: Lowmere

why.founding: The western lake's level swings four metres a year, so its people stopped building on the shore and built on the water instead.
why.siteAdvantages: Sheltered water behind a headland, deep enough never to ground and shallow enough to pole.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay afloat because a rafted village cannot be evicted from land it does not occupy — a point they make often.
why.pressures: Gideon's council has twice tried to tax the lake and twice failed to find the village where it left it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would come ashore only under a threat no council could make.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: floats; needs sheltered water and mooring points
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle

notableNpcSlots: the mooring-holder who decides where the village sits

vibe.silhouette: Thirty low rafts moored in a loose spiral, each with a reed house on it, all of it moving slightly all the time.
vibe.palette: Reed gold, black lake water, and every roof at a slightly different angle.
vibe.materials: Lashed buoyant timber, reed houses, walkways of plank that are untied and retied constantly.
vibe.signatureFeature: The spiral: the village's plan is a mooring order, and the order is social — the centre is the oldest household.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt continuously; no raft is more than fifteen years old.
vibe.mood: Fluid, gossipy, hard to pin down in every sense.
vibe.approach: From the shore it is a low line of roofs on water with no land under it, which reads immediately as different.
vibe.senses: Water under everything; timber knocking; conversation that carries across the whole village.

places.name: Mile House of the Eagle

why.founding: A Legion road-house built one march west of Gideon, kept open because the road still needs a place to stop before the gate closes at dusk.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm, drained ground before the road drops to the flood plain; a walled yard big enough for six carts.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper holds an inherited road-warrant nobody has renewed since the Legions left, and produces it unprompted.
why.pressures: Fort Swampmoth's toll-takers stop here too, and the keeper cannot refuse them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close the first year the road did not carry carts.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road

notableNpcSlots: the keeper with the unrenewed warrant

vibe.silhouette: A long low tiled range with a walled yard, the only straight lines on the ridge.
vibe.palette: Legion red on a repainted door, lichen grey, cart-track ochre.
vibe.materials: Imperial farmhouse masonry with a reed-thatched cart shelter added.
vibe.signatureFeature: The milestone in the yard, still legible, still counting to a city in another province.
vibe.condition: Sound, thriftily maintained, one range shut up and used for hay.
vibe.approach: You see the yard wall from a bend a good half-kilometre out — it is the only masonry between here and the notch.
vibe.senses: Cart axles; a dog; the smell of frying river fish.

places.name: Moonrack

why.founding: Folk alchemy here is a moon-timed craft, and calcining needs a level court laid out to the moons, not to the sun.
why.siteAdvantages: A flat upland shelf with an unobstructed eastern horizon — rare below the rim and worth walking to.
why.occupantsMotive: The two practitioners here sell reagents to Gideon and teach nobody, which is normal.
why.pressures: Their court's alignment is drifting out of true as the shelf slumps, and they are arguing about whether to move.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be rebuilt fifty metres east, entirely, rather than adjusted.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a settlement, above canopy where possible
hardConstraints: a level shelf with an open eastern horizon

occupants: one apprentice who will not be taught
notableNpcSlots: the sign-reader who set the court

vibe.silhouette: A paved circle on an open shelf, with a timber rack of shallow trays turned to face the eastern sky.
vibe.palette: Ash white trays, slate paving, the moon-blue of glazed dishes.
vibe.materials: Laid stone, fired clay dishes, a timber rack — precise where nothing else in the zone is.
vibe.signatureFeature: The rack itself, angled and re-angled, its post holes drilled in a visible arc of past positions.
vibe.condition: Meticulous, swept, subtly out of true.
vibe.mood: Quiet, technical, superstitious in a way that is also empirical.
vibe.approach: The shelf appears above the tree line and the rack breaks its skyline — a close, tall cue.
vibe.senses: Trays scraped; wind on an open shelf; a faint mineral bitterness.

places.name: Nine-Arch Stage

why.founding: A stage grew where the road crosses the flood plain on a nine-arched viaduct, because the crossing takes longer than the daylight left.
why.siteAdvantages: The viaduct's dry undercroft is the only rain-proof shelter for two hours in either direction.
why.occupantsMotive: The family here sells fuel and fodder and charges for the undercroft, which they do not own.
why.pressures: Four arches have silted solid, so the flood now goes over the road rather than under it twice a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the viaduct failed — and it will.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing; something named within 300 m of the road

occupants: D2 road wildlife at the silted arches

vibe.silhouette: Nine arches on a dead-flat plain, four of them full of mud, carrying a road four metres above the water.
vibe.palette: Silt grey, weathered pale mortar, green algae to the flood line.
vibe.materials: Imperial cut-stone arches with reed lean-tos wedged into the piers.
vibe.signatureFeature: The flood scale painted up the third pier, repainted higher three times.
vibe.condition: The road deck is sound; everything below it is being eaten.
vibe.approach: The arches read from a long way across the plain — a rare true sightline in this province, and it is man-made.
vibe.senses: Water sucking at the silted arches; swallows; wind across the deck.

why.founding: A village that exists to rebuild carts, because the road's stone surface destroys wheels made for marsh paths.
why.siteAdvantages: Halfway between the fort and the marsh edge: the exact distance at which the wheels fail.
why.occupantsMotive: Nine families, each with one specialism, refuse to teach each other's trade.
why.pressures: The road surface is breaking up and taking fewer wheels with it, which is bad for Ninefold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a farming village within two generations if the road stone finished failing.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: day-travel spacing along a road

vibe.silhouette: Nine open-sided workshops around a rutted green, each with a different half-finished thing in it.
vibe.palette: Sawdust pale, timber brown, iron-tyre blue-grey.
vibe.materials: Timber frames with reed roofs; the only iron in the village is in the tyre hoop.
vibe.signatureFeature: The wheel fence: failed wheels stood on edge as the village's boundary, hundreds of them.
vibe.condition: Working, sawdust everywhere, roofs excellent because the wrights are also thatchers.
vibe.approach: The wheel fence is visible from the road for two hundred metres and reads as nothing else.
vibe.senses: Adzes; a tyre being shrunk with a hiss; nine different rhythms.

why.founding: A house built against a Legion milestone by a family who found it easier to name themselves after it than to name the place.
why.siteAdvantages: Nine miles from the gate: the distance a loaded porter covers before wanting to stop.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters and pilgrims are the trade; the family sells water, shade and foot-binding.
why.pressures: The pilgrim traffic to Glenbridge has doubled and the well has not.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced by a bigger house on the same spot, which is how every stop on this road grew.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: on the road at porter-stage distance

vibe.silhouette: A single-storey house wrapped around a Legion milestone that now holds up one corner of its porch.
vibe.palette: Whitewash, dust, the deep green of the porch vine.
vibe.materials: Mud brick, reed, and one Imperial stone that predates everything.
vibe.signatureFeature: The milestone in the porch post, its numeral polished by two centuries of people leaning on it.
vibe.condition: Modest, sound, constantly extended by one room.
vibe.approach: The vine is visible from further than the house is.
vibe.senses: Well rope; feet being unwrapped; bees in the vine.

places.name: Onkobra Clay Pits

why.founding: Gideon's red pottery is canon; red pottery means a red clay bank, a water source and a kiln within a cart of the city.
why.siteAdvantages: A cut meander bank exposes the clay in a two-metre seam; the river takes the waste and brings the fuel.
why.occupantsMotive: Four potting families work it in rotation and quarrel about the rotation.
why.pressures: The seam is being undercut by the river it depends on; the wintertide rootworm migration marks its stop with this very clay, and the waykeepers want the bank left alone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move fifty metres upstream, as it has three times before, which is the most Argonian thing about it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: river clay; needs water and fuel
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a navigable water for export
hardConstraints: exposed clay seam at a river bank
preferences: a kiln downwind of the drying floor

notableNpcSlots: the eldest potter, who sets the rotation

vibe.silhouette: A red gash in a green bank, a field of pots drying in ranks, one bottle kiln with a crooked chimney.
vibe.palette: Signal red, dust pink, kiln-soot black, river brown.
vibe.materials: Raw clay, fired clay, reed drying racks and one Imperial-built brick kiln.
vibe.signatureFeature: The seconds wall: two centuries of failed pots pressed into the flood bank as revetment.
vibe.condition: Busy, muddy, permanently rebuilt.
vibe.approach: The path turns and the whole bank is red — the strongest colour for a kilometre in any direction.
vibe.senses: Wet clay; woodsmoke; the ring of pots being tapped for cracks.

places.name: Onkobra Ferry

why.founding: The river below Gideon is too wide to bridge and too useful not to cross.
why.siteAdvantages: A double bend slows the current to polling speed, and both banks shelve gently.
why.occupantsMotive: The ferry family has held the crossing four generations and treats the rope as property.
why.pressures: The bonded warehouse opposite would rather load direct and cut them out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the day a bridge is built, which the council proposes every decade.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: across water too deep or wide to ford
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

notableNpcSlots: the ferrywoman who sets the crossing order

vibe.silhouette: A tarred plank raft on a rope, a slipway of laid brushwood, a shelter with one bench.
vibe.palette: Tar black, river brown, the bright yellow of new brushwood.
vibe.materials: Plank ferry and hemp; the shelter is reed on four poles.
vibe.signatureFeature: The crossing order chalked on the shelter wall — and the standing rule that a comer with a body to carry goes first.
vibe.condition: Working hard, patched, rope replaced more often than anything else.
vibe.approach: The road bends down through willow scrub and the water is suddenly a hundred metres wide.
vibe.senses: Rope creak; water on planks; the ferry bell, once per crossing.

places.name: Onkobra Kwama Mine

why.founding: Dunmer husbandry practised at the far western end of its range, because Gideon will buy eggs and Leyawiin will buy them dearer. The workings themselves changed hands in the 3E uprisings, when the Argonian mine hands took the kwama mines from their Dunmer owners; the husbandry is Dunmer technique kept on by Argonian owners, not Dunmer ownership.
why.siteAdvantages: A limestone shoulder above the Onkobra with dry galleries — the only ground in the west a kwama colony will hold.
why.occupantsMotive: The mining family keeps the queen alive because a dead queen is a dead trade; the Owing hands work it because they were entered in a ledger.
why.pressures: Scribs get out; the colony has been pushed for two hundred years and the eggs are smaller than the ledgers say they should be.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse the year the queen dies, and everyone here knows the date is close.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a road for shipping
hardConstraints: dry gallery ground above the river

occupants: D3 scrib swarms below the second gallery
notableNpcSlots: the mine family's heir who wants out
the tally-clerk from Gideon

vibe.silhouette: A shed, a spoil heap and a black adit in a pale bluff above brown water.
vibe.palette: Chalk-pale rock, ochre spoil, the wet grey-green of kwama chitin.
vibe.materials: Timber head-gear and Imperial cart track; everything underground is unlined rock.
vibe.signatureFeature: The queen's gallery: a domed dig you can stand up in, warm as a byre.
vibe.condition: Overworked, propped, patched with green timber.
vibe.approach: The road smells of the rendering shed a full minute before the adit shows.
vibe.senses: Chitin clicking underfoot; dripping; a low continuous hum from the queen.

why.founding: The obligation to shelter a comer is absolute, so villages maintain a house that is nobody's and everybody's.
why.siteAdvantages: Set at the saddle where four paths meet, so the obligation is discharged where it is most needed.
why.occupantsMotive: It is kept by rota; the family whose month it is stocks it and does not attend it.
why.pressures: Foreigners keep trying to pay, which is understood as an insult and forgiven as ignorance.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a scandal if it were ever found empty of fuel.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

vibe.silhouette: A small round house with no door in the doorway, a fire laid but unlit, on a bare saddle.
vibe.palette: Thatch gold, mud-wall ochre, hearth black.
vibe.materials: Round mud-and-wattle walls, reed roof, a single stone hearth ring.
vibe.signatureFeature: The stocked hearth: fuel, water and dried fish, replenished by strangers for strangers.
vibe.condition: Immaculate; the rota is visible in how new the thatch is.
vibe.approach: It sits on the skyline of the saddle, small and pale, and there is no gate and no wall.
vibe.senses: Wind in the doorway; ash; a very deep quiet.

places.name: Hand-Read Halls
sources: world/sources/lore/topics/lost-peoples.md §Orma (a tribe of Men born without eye sockets; masters of touch; tactile door-marks, no light wells, sound-oriented layouts)

why.founding: The Orma were canon-native to Black Marsh and gone by the late Third Era. They built for people with no eyes, and this is the only Orma work in the province substantial enough to still be read — by hand.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry box canyon in the western hills: enclosed, quiet, and acoustically legible, which for its builders was the whole specification.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. A scholars' camp outside has been at it for two seasons and is measuring the wrong things.
why.pressures: Every visitor brings a lamp, and the lamp is exactly what stops the building working.
why.wouldChangeIf: Anyone who put the light out and followed the ridges would find the chamber, which is the whole design of the place and cannot be brute-forced.

preferences: deliberately isolated — the Orma left almost nothing
a scholars' field camp 200-400 m off

vibe.silhouette: a doorway in a canyon wall with no lintel carving, no window anywhere above it, and two ridges running away into black
vibe.palette: unrelieved dark; dry pale stone at the mouth and nothing after it
vibe.materials: dressed stone with continuous guide-ridges at hand height, texture where a ruin would have ornament
vibe.signatureFeature: A navigation system that still works perfectly in total darkness, in a building that has no provision for light at all.
vibe.condition: structurally sound and completely illegible to a lamp
vibe.mood: a place that was never meant to be looked at
vibe.approach: The scholars' camp is met first, with its charts of an ornament scheme that does not exist.
vibe.senses: chambers proportioned for echo; your own footsteps arriving back changed

places.singularClaim: countBand [1,1]: canon says the Orma left almost nothing — a second site would contradict the source.

places.name: Red Cart Yard

why.founding: Freight changes carriers where the wheeled road ends and the marsh paths begin; somebody organises the change and takes a cut.
why.siteAdvantages: The last hard standing before the ground goes soft — carts cannot go on, porters cannot start earlier.
why.occupantsMotive: The yard master holds the porters' Owing entries, so the labour cannot leave for a better yard.
why.pressures: Two porters have run this year, and the yard master has posted their names.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its purpose if the causeway were ever built to cart standard.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node between a boat lane and a land route

notableNpcSlots: the yard master with the ledger
the porter whose name is on the board

vibe.silhouette: A red-dust yard, a load rack, and a long open shed of hammocks — no walls anywhere.
vibe.palette: Clay red, rope brown, the pale blue of the porters' issued sashes.
vibe.materials: Beaten earth, a timber load rack, reed shade, one lockable ledger box.
vibe.signatureFeature: The runaway board: two names, painted, with the amount still owed under each.
vibe.condition: Hard-used, swept, deliberately comfortless.
vibe.approach: Cart noise stops; the road becomes a path; the yard is the hinge.
vibe.senses: Hammock ropes; a tally counted aloud; dust.

places.name: Red Daub Relay

why.founding: The province's letters move by running couriers, and a run has to break where the ground changes.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road path meets the marsh path, with red clay daubed on the trees to mark it for people who cannot read.
why.occupantsMotive: The runners hold the relay because the office is inherited and carries the right to refuse a letter.
why.pressures: The council wants the letters read; the runners regard that as the one thing they will not do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse if the running families ever agreed to be paid by the council instead of the senders.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

notableNpcSlots: the relay elder who refuses letters

vibe.silhouette: A post, a covered box on legs, a hammock frame, and red daub on twelve trees around it.
vibe.palette: Clay red marks, bark grey, hammock indigo.
vibe.materials: A waxed letter box, reed shelter, nothing lockable.
vibe.signatureFeature: The refusal peg: letters the relay will not carry, hung on a peg for the sender to reclaim.
vibe.condition: Minimal, maintained daily.
vibe.approach: You notice the daub marks first and follow them in; the marks are the wayfinding system.
vibe.senses: Cicadas; someone leaving at a run.

why.founding: A village-built floating timber bridge on the reed road, tolled in reed bundles rather than coin.
why.siteAdvantages: A slow, shallow reach where a buoyant causeway can be moored rather than piled.
why.occupantsMotive: The cutters maintain it themselves and take their toll in the one thing they need and cannot carry far.
why.pressures: Coin-payers are charged more, which foreigners find funny until they understand it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be untied and floated away if a tax-taker ever tried to farm it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: spans a channel at its narrowest
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the route graph; its owner lives within sight

vibe.silhouette: A dark timber raft-bridge lying almost flush on the water, sagging under anyone who crosses.
vibe.palette: Reed gold, black wet timber, tea-coloured water.
vibe.materials: Buoyant lashed timber, reed fenders, no metal at all.
vibe.signatureFeature: The bundle post: the toll, stacked as cut reed, restacked daily.
vibe.condition: Constantly repaired, never rebuilt; no part of it is older than four years.
vibe.approach: You hear it before you see it — the whole deck knocks against itself in any wind.
vibe.senses: Timber knocking; reed rustle; wet rope.

why.founding: The rim route between Gideon and the north is faster than the road and no cart can use it, so letters go that way and nothing else does.
why.siteAdvantages: A saddle high enough that a runner can see the next saddle — one of the very few places in the province where that is true.
why.occupantsMotive: Runners use it because it halves the time to Stormhold; nobody else uses it because it is a scramble.
why.pressures: One bad section is washing out and the runners argue about whether to say so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be lost in a season if the runners stopped clearing it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay
hardConstraints: a saddle with a line to the next saddle

vibe.silhouette: A drystone wind shelter the height of a crouching person, and a cairn with cloth tied to it.
vibe.palette: Rock grey, cloth faded to no colour, sky.
vibe.materials: Dry stone and knotted cloth. Nothing else is carried up here.
vibe.signatureFeature: The knot record: each runner ties one knot passing through, and the cairn cloth is read as a tally.
vibe.condition: Weathered, rebuilt after every storm.
vibe.approach: You come up out of a ravine and can suddenly see for two kilometres — a rarity worth the climb.
vibe.senses: Wind; cloth snapping; nothing else at all.

places.name: Rockgrove
sources: uesp:Lore:Rockgrove (the Ca-Uxith, the stone-talkers, the geyser field)

why.founding: A Sul-Xan holding in the Blackwood: a staging ground for raids that take souls rather than goods.
why.siteAdvantages: Screened by jungle on three sides, one ravine path in, and a stream that hides the noise of a camp.
why.occupantsMotive: The Sul-Xan raid to feed soul-snares; the site persists because it has never been found twice by the same people.
why.pressures: Stonewastes' Four Winds hunt them; the Empire's old bounty on jade masks is still quoted in Gideon. The Sul-Xan are not alone on this ground: the Ca-Uxith are charged by their Hist with watching the xanmeer, and their stone-talkers hold the ruins against the geyser field beneath it — the raid camp sits on top of somebody else's duty.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move within a season of a serious defeat — the camp is the people, not the ground.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: within raiding distance of villages

notableNpcSlots: the mask-bearer

vibe.silhouette: Nothing at all until the tree line, then hide tents under a jade-green canopy and poles hung with masks.
vibe.palette: Jade, blood-brown, deep shadow-green.
vibe.materials: Hide, lashed poles, jade death masks, no permanent structure whatsoever.
vibe.signatureFeature: The snare rack: soul-gems strung on cord at head height so raiders walk under them.
vibe.condition: Temporary by design, filthy, meticulously ordered where the trophies are.
vibe.approach: A raiders' path along a stream bed, then green tattoos in the leaves at ten metres.
vibe.senses: Low chanting; flies; the hum of charged gems.

places.name: Saddle Fair

why.founding: Gideon's gate tax made it cheaper to trade outside the walls, so the trade went outside the walls.
why.siteAdvantages: The flat saddle floor a kilometre west of the gate: level, drained, and legally nowhere.
why.occupantsMotive: Traders come because there is no tax; the council tolerates it because it can watch the whole field from the wall.
why.pressures: Every few years the council tries to enclose it, and every few years the fair moves two hundred metres.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be inside the city within a decade if the gate tax were dropped.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a landing, because most goods come by water
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on neutral ground between settlements, or in an M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: level drained ground outside a city's jurisdiction

occupants: D1 traders and crowds in season
notableNpcSlots: the fair-reeve elected for the week

vibe.silhouette: In season: two hundred striped awnings in a shallow bowl below the city wall. Out of season: worn rings in the turf.
vibe.palette: Awning stripes in madder and indigo against grey-green turf and the city's red tiles above.
vibe.materials: Market tents, hurdles, tethering lines — nothing that outlasts the week.
vibe.signatureFeature: The pitch rings: bare circles in the grass showing exactly who has traded here longest.
vibe.condition: Nothing permanent, by law and by preference.
vibe.approach: You come over the saddle lip and the whole fair is below you at once — the zone's best single reveal.
vibe.senses: Auction calling; guar; frying oil; three languages.

places.name: Silver Mouth

why.founding: A Kothringi river town that emptied inside one season in 2E 560 and was never entered again.
why.siteAdvantages: A river mouth on the lake with the only stone quay in the west — the Kothringi built to last, which is why it is still here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the neighbouring villages regard the ground as still infectious, three hundred years on.
why.pressures: The quay is the best landing on the lake and the taboo is the only reason it is unused.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be occupied within a year if a single respected voice said the ground was clean.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: coastal and riverine — they were sea-going
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the west and centre, where the Kothringi lived
hardConstraints: a stone quay at a river mouth

occupants: D3 in the flooded lower streets

vibe.silhouette: A stone quay and three parallel streets of roofless houses running down into the lake.
vibe.palette: Silver-grey stone, lake blue-black, and a total absence of green on the paving.
vibe.materials: Kothringi coursed stone — squarer, finer and older than anything Imperial in the province.
vibe.signatureFeature: The streets continue underwater; you can follow the same street diving.
vibe.condition: Roofless, walls standing to two storeys, absolutely undisturbed.
vibe.approach: By boat it appears all at once as a stone shore in a province with no stone shores.
vibe.senses: Water in stone doorways; a hollow echo; unusually few birds.

why.founding: The Kothringi buried under stone, and this hillside holds a whole community's worth from the last generation before the Flu.
why.siteAdvantages: A stony hill shoulder where cairn stone lay ready to hand — the only reason the site is here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it; Argonian custom has no use for it and there are no Kothringi left to disagree.
why.pressures: Treasure-hunters take the glass beads; the practice is old enough that some cairns have been opened twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be protected if anyone in the province had standing to protect a dead people's graves.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: beside a lost-peoples ruin
preferences: a hillside with cairns visible against the sky

vibe.silhouette: Two hundred stone mounds on an open hillside, a third of them opened and spilled downhill.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, pale grass, and glints of blue-green glass in the spoil.
vibe.materials: Dry-stacked local stone; the glass beads are the only worked thing here.
vibe.signatureFeature: The opened cairns: their stones lie downslope in fans, so the hillside reads as damage from a distance.
vibe.condition: Two thirds intact, one third robbed and never reclosed.
vibe.approach: One of the zone's few genuine long views — the mounds break the skyline from the valley track.
vibe.senses: Wind over stones; glass grinding underfoot; nothing living.

places.name: Slough Point

why.founding: The Empire put its census and excise station where the Blackwood Road first touches navigable water, so goods could be counted twice.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank at the head of a slow reach: carts arrive, boats leave, and the two must be weighed against each other somewhere.
why.occupantsMotive: The excise remains because whoever collects it eats; the census remains because the ledgers are the only proof anyone here exists.
why.pressures: Everything worth taxing now goes by the rim paths instead; the town's takings fall every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would die if the road were abandoned, or become rich again if a state ever taxed the marsh in earnest.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the province's border; one of only three or four
hardConstraints: a place to hold carts overnight

notableNpcSlots: the tallyman who remembers every cart
the ferryman who is also a smuggler

vibe.silhouette: A weighbridge, a long bonded shed and a jetty, strung out along one street with no middle.
vibe.palette: Whitewashed lime going green, tar-black sheds, brown water.
vibe.materials: Imperial farmhouse timber-and-plaster; Argonian reed roofs on everything built since.
vibe.signatureFeature: The census board outside the excise house, names still being added in three scripts.
vibe.condition: Working, shabby, over-built for its traffic.
vibe.approach: You smell the tar sheds before you see the roofs; the road simply widens into the town.
vibe.senses: Tally sticks, dripping tar, a bell for the ferry.

why.founding: Slough Point's excise came with a census, and a census in a province that remembers the Knahaten Flu means an inspection shed.
why.siteAdvantages: On the landing, before the weighbridge — nothing passes inland unlooked-at.
why.occupantsMotive: The inspectors keep it because the fee for release is theirs; nobody has been detained in living memory.
why.pressures: The forms still ask questions about a plague that ended two centuries ago, in a script most comers cannot read.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be repurposed as a store the day the excise lapsed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: at a legal port or border crossing
hardConstraints: at a landing, before the customs point

vibe.silhouette: A slat-sided shed on the landing with benches down both walls and a smoking brazier in the middle.
vibe.palette: Smoke-stained timber, brazier red, the green of the river through the slats.
vibe.materials: Timber slats, a stone brazier plinth, an Imperial noticeboard nobody has updated.
vibe.signatureFeature: The form: an Imperial plague questionnaire, still issued, still in Cyrodiilic.
vibe.condition: Sound, sooty, over-provided with benches.
vibe.approach: It is the first building off the jetty; you cannot avoid it and that is the design.
vibe.senses: Smoke; a stamp; river slapping the piles.

places.name: Stonefoot

why.founding: Upland Argonians terrace, because the hills are the only ground in the province where terracing is possible at all.
why.siteAdvantages: A south-facing slope above the ravine head, with spring water at the top and stone to build the terraces from.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because terraces are generational work and abandoning them wastes four lifetimes.
why.pressures: Using stone for the terrace walls is a compromise the lowland villages needle them about constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse literally and socially if the spring at the top failed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a pass or an upland route; isolated
hardConstraints: a south-facing slope with a spring above

occupants: D3 rim wildlife above the top wall
notableNpcSlots: the water-holder who allocates the spring

vibe.silhouette: Twenty stone-walled terraces stepping up a hillside with a house at the end of every third one.
vibe.palette: Dry-stone grey, terrace-crop green in bands, brown earth between.
vibe.materials: Dry stone below, mud and reed above — the only village in the zone that builds in two materials by height.
vibe.signatureFeature: The water ladder: a stone channel running down the terrace ends, with a wooden gate at each level.
vibe.condition: Superbly maintained; a fallen terrace wall is a village emergency.
vibe.approach: The banding of the terraces reads from the valley floor at a kilometre — the zone's most legible settlement.
vibe.senses: Water running down the ladder; goats; stone being reset.

places.name: Stonewastes

why.founding: A bogland town that grew around a xanmeer keep its people never stopped using, defended since their ancestors raised their first hut by the hereditary Four Winds.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls that already existed, on the only firm ground in a bog nobody else can cross quickly.
why.occupantsMotive: The Four Winds hold the keep because holding it is who they are; the Sul-Xan raiding out of the Blackwood is why the office never lapsed.
why.pressures: Four hereditary captains and one gate is three captains too many; the Sul-Xan press harder each dry season.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change utterly if the Four Winds ever accepted an outside charter — which is exactly what the Marsh Charter will ask of them.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: defensible approach, often a single crossing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the Blackwood bogland's only defended town; Glenbridge a day south

occupants: one very strong D4 senior captain
notableNpcSlots: the four captains
the keep's Hist-minder

vibe.silhouette: A stepped stone keep rising out of low mud-and-thatch roofs, with four banner poles on the terrace, one per wind.
vibe.palette: Bog-brown, grey-green stone, four dyed banners in ochre, indigo, white and black.
vibe.materials: Ancient xanmeer masonry the villagers maintain but do not imitate; everything they build themselves is mud, wattle and thatch.
vibe.signatureFeature: The Four Winds' drill ground on the keep terrace, worn into the stone in four wheel-shaped paths.
vibe.condition: Impeccably kept where it is stone, deliberately impermanent where it is not.
vibe.mood: Martial, proud, closed to strangers and formally courteous to them.
vibe.approach: The causeway runs straight at the keep for four hundred metres with bog on both sides — you are watched the whole way.
vibe.senses: Drill counting; wet thatch; a hollow drum used as a gate signal.

places.name: Swampmoth Town

why.founding: A garrison feeds, drinks and buys, so a town grows below its gate whether or not the garrison is legitimate.
why.siteAdvantages: The apron of firm ground below the fort's ridge, inside the arc the fort can protect.
why.occupantsMotive: The town lives off the toll company and is embarrassed about it in public and not in private.
why.pressures: If the tolls fail, the town starves; if the tolls succeed, the town is complicit. It has chosen.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would survive as a road village at a third the size — which is what it was before.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: at a crossing or a road
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with a fort, occupied or not
hardConstraints: below a held fort, within its protective arc

notableNpcSlots: the victualler who bankrolls the company
the smith who will not shoe their guar

vibe.silhouette: One street of shuttered fronts under a fort wall, every roof lower than the curtain above it.
vibe.palette: Wall-shadow grey for half the day, then hard light; painted shutters; rust.
vibe.materials: Mud-brick and timber built tight against Imperial masonry it is not bonded to.
vibe.signatureFeature: The shadow line on the street, which the townsfolk time their day by.
vibe.condition: Cramped, prosperous, built too close to the wall to be safe.
vibe.approach: You come up the road under the fort and the town is a strip of roofs in its shadow.
vibe.senses: Boots on stone above; a smithy; shutters closing when the company comes down.

why.founding: Nisswo doctrine holds that a made thing must be unmade, and pilgrims on the sermon road need somewhere to do it.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel spit in a river bend: a flat working floor that the flood clears entirely every year.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims make something here and destroy it; the site's whole content is what has not been destroyed yet.
why.pressures: Collectors have started stealing pieces before they can be unmade, which is theologically catastrophic and commercially excellent.
