why.wouldChangeIf: Would be spoiled permanently if a piece from here were ever displayed in Gideon.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a Nisswo circuit
hardConstraints: a working floor the flood clears annually

vibe.silhouette: A gravel spit covered in half-finished sculpture, and a burn patch at one end with ash a foot deep.
vibe.palette: Grey gravel, ash white, and whatever colours today's pieces are.
vibe.materials: Clay, reed, bone, river stone — everything is made from what is on the spit.
vibe.signatureFeature: The ash end: a year of destroyed work in one heap, which is the actual monument.
vibe.condition: Nothing here is more than a year old, by doctrine and by flood.
vibe.approach: You see the colour of the pieces from upstream before you can make out what they are.
vibe.senses: River on gravel; clay being worked; something being broken deliberately.

places.name: The Back Kiln

why.founding: A disused pottery kiln outside the clay pits became the place where Gideon does what it cannot do inside the walls.
why.siteAdvantages: A domed brick chamber that holds heat, hides light, and has one door — ideal for exactly one purpose.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper pays the tower clerk to record the site as derelict, and it is, on paper.
why.pressures: Owing enforcers recruit here; so do people organising against them, on different nights.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be burned out by the council the week it became embarrassing rather than useful.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a mooring is half the type
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who is on three payrolls

vibe.silhouette: A brick beehive in a nettle field with light leaking from one low doorway and no chimney smoke.
vibe.palette: Soot black, ember orange, nettle green.
vibe.materials: Fired brick, reed baffles over the flue, cushions that came out of somebody's estate.
vibe.signatureFeature: The stacked seconds inside — the room is furnished entirely with failed pots.
vibe.condition: Structurally fine and deliberately unmaintained-looking outside.
vibe.approach: There is no path to it; you follow the trodden nettles.
vibe.senses: Low voices amplified by the dome; dice; sap-smoke.

why.founding: A deep cold tarn in a rim basin holds something old, and the villages' rule about it predates their oldest stories.
why.siteAdvantages: A drowned box canyon: sheer walls, forty metres of cold water, one narrow outlet.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing human lives here. The rule is that you may drink from the outlet and not from the tarn.
why.pressures: Treasure-hunters ignore the rule roughly once a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change. That is what fixed danger means; the province will not soften it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the apex hazard of its region; routes bend around it
hardConstraints: deep cold water in a closed basin
preferences: a drinking place at the outlet

vibe.silhouette: Black water in a stone bowl, absolutely still, with a pale drinking step at the one outlet.
vibe.palette: Black, stone grey, and one white line of outflow.
vibe.materials: Nothing built but the drinking step, worn hollow, at a careful distance from the water.
vibe.signatureFeature: The step's position: deliberately at the outlet, deliberately not at the tarn.
vibe.condition: Timeless. Nothing here has changed and nothing will.
vibe.approach: A climb into a bowl, and then water that is a different colour from any other water in the province.
vibe.senses: The outflow; no birds on the water; no insects over it.

why.founding: An Imperial road villa emptied two centuries ago, and one family has been living in three of its rooms for two generations.
why.siteAdvantages: It is dry, roofed, and off the road behind a hedge that has become a wall.
why.occupantsMotive: They live here because it is free; they have built a reed house inside the atrium rather than use the rooms as rooms.
why.pressures: Living in dead stone is a compromise their neighbours mention, and the reed house inside is their answer to it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned without regret the day the roof went.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: inside any ruin type

vibe.silhouette: A villa's tiled roof over a hedge, and inside its courtyard a reed house with its own little roof.
vibe.palette: Terracotta above, reed gold within, hedge green all around.
vibe.materials: Imperial masonry used as a shell; the actual dwelling inside it is entirely reed and mud.
vibe.signatureFeature: The house inside the house — the province's material ethics as domestic architecture.
vibe.condition: The Imperial fabric is failing; the reed house is new.
vibe.approach: The hedge hides it entirely; you find it by a path through a gap.
vibe.senses: Chickens in a peristyle; rain on tiles and then on reed; two roofs at once.

places.name: The Buried Spears
sources: uesp:Lore:Blackwater War (1E 2836: the Argonians stop fighting and bury their weapons)

why.founding: When the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War they buried their weapons rather than surrendering them.
why.siteAdvantages: Under a bank of dry sand above the flood line, where iron would keep — chosen by people who expected to come back.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody has come back. The location is passed on as a story with directions in it.
why.pressures: The Owing brokers would pay for the location; so would the Marsh Charter, for opposite reasons.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious political object the day anyone dug it up.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a battlefield or a village of the period
preferences: a marker no outsider would read

vibe.silhouette: A sand bank under three trees, with one tree carved at head height in a mark that means nothing to foreigners.
vibe.palette: Sand pale, bark grey, leaf shadow.
vibe.materials: Nothing built. The cache is bundled hide and pitch, and the marker is a carving.
vibe.signatureFeature: The carving: a Jel word for 'enough', which is the whole history of the war in one cut.
vibe.condition: Undisturbed; the pitch has held.
vibe.mood: Ordinary, until you know; then heavy.
vibe.approach: It is invisible. You arrive with directions from a story or you never arrive.
vibe.senses: Wind in three trees; sand; nothing to hear at all.

places.name: The Cold Forge

why.founding: Somebody in the west still works iron, because the road runs on iron tyres and nobody else will touch it.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the bog-iron workings and downwind of everything, because the neighbours insisted.
why.occupantsMotive: The smith is Imperial-trained, Argonian-born, and equally unwelcome in both explanations of himself.
why.pressures: Working metal is a moral error to most of his neighbours; they still bring him their tyres.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close the day the road did, and he would be relieved.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a road, in a port, or hidden

occupants: a striker who does not speak
notableNpcSlots: the smith

vibe.silhouette: A stone-built forge with a tall chimney, standing alone in cleared ground with no house nearer than a kilometre.
vibe.palette: Charcoal black, forge orange, the scoured pale of cleared ground.
vibe.materials: Cut stone and iron — the only building in the zone made of the two things the province distrusts.
vibe.signatureFeature: The offering shelf outside the door, where neighbours leave work and payment without entering.
vibe.condition: Excellent. Nothing here is patched, which is itself unusual.
vibe.approach: The chimney smoke is the cue; you smell charcoal a long way before you see it.
vibe.senses: Hammer on anvil, arriving in pairs; the bellows; quenching.

places.name: The Cold Lights
sources: docs/research/settlement-type-recipes.md (lit cues; sound and light as wayfinding)

why.founding: A cold spring feeds one arm of the lake, and whatever lives in it lights when it is disturbed.
why.siteAdvantages: A dead-end arm with no current, where the bloom is never flushed out.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody owns it; the raft village uses it to navigate at night and treats it as a shared instrument.
why.pressures: It is dimmer than it was, and the village argues about whether that is the spring or the lake.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious loss, practically as well as aesthetically, if it failed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: known and visited; a destination, not a secret
hardConstraints: still water fed by a cold spring

vibe.silhouette: Black water that lights blue-green where a paddle touches it, and stays lit for a few seconds behind you.
vibe.palette: Black and one blue-green, and nothing else after dark.
vibe.materials: Nothing built; there is a single pole at the arm's mouth to find it by.
vibe.signatureFeature: Your own wake, glowing, marking exactly where you have been.
vibe.condition: Undiminished from a distance; measurably dimmer up close.
vibe.approach: By day the arm is unremarkable. Everything about this place is a night reveal.
vibe.senses: Almost nothing — the silence is what makes the light land.

why.founding: A line of marker stones set across the western approaches during the Knahaten Flu, to say which side of the line the living were on.
why.siteAdvantages: Follows the natural contour where the ground firms up — the line a fleeing population would take anyway.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody has moved a stone in three hundred years, and villages still do not build across it.
why.pressures: The stones are being lost one by one to root-heave, and nobody has a record of where they were.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be forgotten entirely in another century, which is the only thing the villages agree it should not do.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: uses water as part of the line where it can
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field
hardConstraints: a contour line of set stones
preferences: a gap where a road crosses

vibe.silhouette: Waist-high stones every hundred paces along a contour, running out of sight in both directions.
vibe.palette: Lichen orange on grey, grass, nothing else.
vibe.materials: Undressed local stone, set upright — a use of stone the province permits because it names the dead.
vibe.signatureFeature: The road gap: two stones set closer together where a path crosses, with a rubbed hollow between them.
vibe.condition: Weathered, several fallen, one recently re-erected by somebody.
vibe.mood: Sober, quiet, cumulative — the impact is in walking along it.
vibe.approach: You cross it without noticing and then see the next stone, and the next.
vibe.senses: Wind; grass; your own footsteps for a long time.

places.name: Counts-The-Dead

why.founding: The Flu killed faster than the dead could be carried home, so the western road villages made one ground and counted into it.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the road, so that anyone carrying bones west has somewhere to stop before the last stage.
why.occupantsMotive: A bone-carrier's office is hereditary here; the current holder keeps the count in her head and on stakes.
why.pressures: The count is still rising, because Owing deaths and burn-country deaths are added to it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close if a court ever ruled that the road's dead had somewhere else to go.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village
hardConstraints: on a road, on ground that takes bone

notableNpcSlots: the hereditary counter

vibe.silhouette: A field of thin stakes, thousands of them, each with a story cut into it, leaning at every angle.
vibe.palette: Weathered stake grey, cut-wood pale where a stake is new, black soil.
vibe.materials: Grave-stakes and one reed shelter; the province's signature system at scale, and nothing else built.
vibe.signatureFeature: The new stakes at the road edge: the field grows towards the road, so the newest are the ones you pass.
vibe.condition: Continuously maintained; the oldest stakes at the far end have rotted to stumps.
vibe.mood: Vast, personal, unbearable in the specific.
vibe.approach: The stakes appear beside the road gradually and you are inside the field before you understand its size.
vibe.senses: Wood knocking on wood in wind — thousands of stakes at once.

places.name: Drowned Furrow
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (no cash-crop economy is possible)

why.founding: A second grant, worked by a family who ploughed the way they had at home and drained nothing.
why.siteAdvantages: The site is superb for eight months and under half a metre of water for four.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody is here; the marsh took the fields and the family went back to Leyawiin without selling.
why.pressures: The house is sound and the neighbours will not use it, because a house whose owners may return is not theirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be reoccupied instantly by anyone from outside the local etiquette — which is the hook.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: tried to be dry and failed
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: strung along a road at Imperial spacing, not local spacing

occupants: D2 water snakes in the byre

vibe.silhouette: A tiled roof standing in a sheet of water, its fields visible as pale ridges under the surface.
vibe.palette: Sky reflected everywhere, terracotta above it, the sick yellow of drowned grass.
vibe.materials: Imperial masonry to sill height in water; nothing local has been added, which is the tell.
vibe.signatureFeature: The plough ridges, still perfectly parallel, three centimetres under.
vibe.condition: Weathertight and utterly unused.
vibe.approach: In the dry season it is an ordinary empty farm; in the wet it is a roof in a lake, and that is when to see it.
vibe.senses: Water lapping in a doorway; a shutter; no birds indoors.

why.founding: A carters' house at the wet end of the road, named for the animal the flood took the year it opened.
why.siteAdvantages: The last building on firm ground before the drowning gate; carters stop here whether they want to or not.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper survives on the wet season, when the road closes and forty carters are stuck for a week.
why.pressures: In a dry year it nearly starves, so the keeper prays for floods and says so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate if the barrier moved, and the sign would go with it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: last firm ground before a seasonal closure

vibe.silhouette: A wide low house with a stilted floor, a stone stable, and a sign carved as a mule underwater.
vibe.palette: Smoke-brown timber, flood-stain grey on the stable, one bright repainted sign.
vibe.materials: Argonian stilt frame with an Imperial stone stable bolted onto the end.
vibe.signatureFeature: The flood lines scored inside the common room, each with a year, the highest above the door.
vibe.condition: Sturdy, damp, cheerfully resigned.
vibe.mood: Crowded and idle, in the way of people who cannot leave.
vibe.approach: The road runs out into water; the house is on the last dry metre with all its lamps lit.
vibe.senses: Rain; cards; wet harness steaming by the fire.

places.name: The Drowning Gate
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (the road closes in the monsoon)

why.founding: Canon closes the Blackwood Road in the monsoon; something has to close it, and this is where.
why.siteAdvantages: The road's lowest point, where the plain drains across it — the water arrives here first and leaves last.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families are paid by Gideon to swing the barrier and to argue with whoever wants it opened anyway.
why.pressures: Every wet season somebody drives round the barrier and drowns; the tally board says how many.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be unnecessary if the Empire's raised causeway had ever been finished — see the drowned embankment beside it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a road that has a wet-season alternative

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who keeps the drowning tally

vibe.silhouette: A painted pole barrier across an empty road with water on both sides for half the year, and nothing at all around it.
vibe.palette: Warning ochre and black bands, brown floodwater, grey sky.
vibe.materials: One Imperial gauge post, a timber boom, a reed hut on stilts.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tally board: a name and a year for every person who went round the barrier.
vibe.condition: Crude, functional, repainted annually.
vibe.approach: In the dry season it looks absurd — a barrier in a field. In the wet you cannot see the road at all.
vibe.senses: Rain on water; the boom creaking; frogs at a volume that makes conversation hard.

why.founding: The Onkobra's upper river drops through eight ledges in a kilometre, which is where boats stop and portage starts.
why.siteAdvantages: A confined reach with rock ledges — the hydrology makes the hazard and the hazard makes the trade.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives in it; the portage families live above and below it and both claim the whole.
why.pressures: Someone runs it every year on a bet and roughly every third one dies.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a route rather than a wall if anyone cut a proper portage path, which is a season's work nobody funds.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: forces every boat route to stop; a portage or a ferry always answers it
hardConstraints: a confined reach with successive ledges
preferences: a portage line on one bank
a memorial at the worst step

vibe.silhouette: Eight white steps in a green-black river between rock walls, with a worn path scrambling beside them.
vibe.palette: White, black rock, and a green so dark it reads as black in shade.
vibe.materials: Nothing built but the portage path and stakes at the worst step.
vibe.signatureFeature: The fourth step, which is the one that kills, marked with grave-stakes on both banks.
vibe.condition: The path is eroding; the stakes are renewed.
vibe.approach: You hear the reach long before the track reaches it, and the sound changes at each step.
vibe.senses: Eight different pitches of white noise; wet rock; nothing else audible.

places.name: Drowned Embankment
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (Imperial roads, bridges and drainage made freight slower)

why.founding: An Imperial scheme to raise the road above the flood, begun with foreign engineering and no local hydrology.
why.siteAdvantages: It runs dead straight across the plain, which is exactly why it failed: it dammed the drainage it crossed.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the villages downstream have been cutting gaps in it for two hundred years.
why.pressures: Each cut gap makes the next flood worse somewhere else, and the arguments about which gap to close are inherited.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a fine road if anyone rebuilt it with culverts — which is what the unfinished culvert line was for.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the line of an abandoned Imperial road
hardConstraints: a straight raised bank across drainage
preferences: standing water on the upstream side

occupants: D2 waterfowl and something in the ponded water

vibe.silhouette: A perfectly straight green ridge across a plain, broken by seven deliberate gaps.
vibe.palette: Grass green on the bank, black standing water on one side, dry cracked mud on the other.
vibe.materials: Rammed earth over an Imperial stone core, exposed where the gaps were cut.
vibe.signatureFeature: The asymmetry: deep water on the upstream face, dust on the downstream, along its whole length.
vibe.condition: Abandoned mid-build; the last two hundred metres are only staked out.
vibe.approach: It reads as a horizon line from anywhere on the plain and never resolves into anything.
vibe.senses: Wind over grass; the flat slap of water on one side only.

why.founding: A river station built by a family who left for Leyawiin in the last bad flood and did not return.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank at a channel junction with its own landing, a walled yard and a well — everything a holding needs and nobody in it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The neighbours have agreed it can be claimed, and have not agreed by whom.
why.pressures: Two villages and the Owing brokers all have a colourable claim; the question has been open four years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would settle the moment somebody credible moved in and made the case — which is exactly the offer.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one per region packet, near but not in a settlement
hardConstraints: a defensible bank at a channel junction

vibe.silhouette: A walled yard with a sound roof, a landing with two rotted piles, and a door standing open.
vibe.palette: Weathered timber, yard-weed green, and the clean stone of a well head that still works.
vibe.materials: Argonian stilt-and-mud construction on a stone footing, unusually well founded, and empty.
vibe.signatureFeature: The open door: nobody has closed it in four years, because closing it would be a claim.
vibe.condition: Sound and deteriorating at exactly the rate an unoccupied building does.
vibe.mood: Expectant. It is a building waiting to be argued over.
vibe.approach: It shows from the channel as a roofline with no smoke, which in this province is the loudest possible signal.
vibe.senses: Wind through an open door; the well rope; nothing else.

places.name: The Fig and Ledger

why.founding: Court business generates waiting, and waiting generates a house that sells wine to people who are waiting.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly outside Gideon's courthouse gate, in the shade of the one old fig on the street.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper sells information as readily as wine and has never been caught selling it twice.
why.pressures: Advocates and fences drink in the same room by unspoken arrangement, and it holds until it doesn't.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close if the courthouse ever stopped sitting — the whole trade is adjournments.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who remembers verdicts

vibe.silhouette: A narrow two-storey house with a fig growing out of the pavement and through the balcony.
vibe.palette: Wine red shutters, fig green, courthouse grey opposite.
vibe.materials: Imperial townhouse masonry, reed awnings, a floor of Onkobra tiles laid by someone who was paid in wine.
vibe.signatureFeature: The adjournment board by the door, listing which cases were put off today.
vibe.condition: Well kept at the front, structurally optimistic at the back.
vibe.approach: It is the first door past the court gate; you do not find it, you are washed into it.
vibe.senses: Argument; cups; figs dropping on the awning.

why.founding: Gideon buys hide and meat and does not ask which side of the village boundaries it came from.
why.siteAdvantages: A dense fig thicket in a ravine head — no sightlines in, water, and three ways out.
why.occupantsMotive: The poachers are village men working a second season's income and would be recognised in daylight.
why.pressures: The village whose ground they work has begun setting its own watch, and there will be a confrontation.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fold immediately if Gideon's market ever asked for provenance.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: just outside a village's watched ground
hardConstraints: dense cover at a ravine head
preferences: a drying rack out of the wind

vibe.silhouette: Drying racks strung between fig trunks, a fire trench dug so the smoke spreads, no tents at all.
vibe.palette: Fig green, meat red, smoke grey held down under the canopy.
vibe.materials: Rope, racks and a dug fire trench — nothing that could not be abandoned in five minutes.
vibe.signatureFeature: The smoke trench: dug and baffled so the fire cannot be seen from above or smelled downhill.
vibe.condition: Reused every season, cleaned between.
vibe.approach: There is no cue. You find it by following a drag trail, or by being brought.
vibe.senses: Dogs kept quiet; flies; smoke that never rises.

places.name: The Glass Scar
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (Argonians invaded Oblivion through the gates)

why.founding: A gate opened on the Blackwood frontier in 4E 5–7 and the Argonians went through it rather than away from it.
why.siteAdvantages: The scar sits on the flat by the road, because that is where the gate stood and gates did not choose ground.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the villages leave it because the ground has never grown back properly.
why.pressures: The Synod wants to survey it, the villages will not permit it, and the argument is annual.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be entirely overgrown by now anywhere else in the province, which is the disturbing part.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near settlements that existed in 3E 433
hardConstraints: a sterile circle of fused ground
preferences: an offering line at the rim

occupants: D3 at the centre after dark

vibe.silhouette: A circle of black fused ground forty metres across, with a rim of offerings around it and nothing growing inside.
vibe.palette: Obsidian black, offering-cloth red, the green that stops dead at the rim.
vibe.materials: Fused earth and glassy slag; the only worked thing is the offering line the villages maintain.
vibe.signatureFeature: The rim: a ring of small offerings, renewed, marking where people will and will not step.
vibe.condition: Unchanged in two centuries.
vibe.mood: Silent, avoided, respected rather than feared.
vibe.approach: The colour break reads from a hundred metres and from nowhere further, in classic Argonian short-range fashion.
vibe.senses: Nothing — no insects at all inside the circle, which is what people notice.

why.founding: A rim scarp with south-facing ledges and thermals is a hackwing colony whether anyone likes it or not.
why.siteAdvantages: Broken cliff ledges above a warm slope; the birds have used it long enough to whiten the rock.
why.occupantsMotive: The birds are here for the updraught; the villages below are here despite them.
why.pressures: Lambing season and hatching season coincide, which is the whole relationship.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change; the colony is older than the villages.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: downwind of a lair, a battlefield or a midden

vibe.silhouette: A cliff face streaked white for eighty metres, with birds turning above it all day.
vibe.palette: Guano white on red-grey rock, and a constantly moving mass of dark wings.
vibe.materials: Nothing built; there is one old rope anchor from someone who once took eggs.
vibe.signatureFeature: The white streaking, which makes the scarp the most visible natural feature on the rim.
vibe.condition: Unchanging.
vibe.approach: Visible from the valley for two kilometres — the white does what no stone here does.
vibe.senses: Continuous shrieking; wind; a smell that arrives before the sound.

places.name: Hollow Pass Station

why.founding: The rim path from Gideon to the north crosses one saddle where a person caught by weather will die, so there is a station on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle's lee side, in a natural hollow that breaks the wind from three directions.
why.occupantsMotive: Two keepers hold it on a season's rota from the villages below, for food and standing.
why.pressures: The path is used more each year by couriers and smugglers, and the station is provisioned for neither number.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the year the rim path lost its traffic to a safer road, which does not exist.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the only crossings of the rim; each one is strategically singular

occupants: D3 on the pass itself in weather

vibe.silhouette: A low turf-roofed building in a hollow, with a horn on a post at the saddle's crest above it.
vibe.palette: Turf green on the roof, stone grey, and above the crest, cloud most days.
vibe.materials: Dry stone with a turf roof, so from above it is invisible and from below it is a green lump.
vibe.signatureFeature: The horn: sounded when weather comes over, and the only sound that carries on that ground.
vibe.condition: Thick-walled, sound, buried in its own hollow.
vibe.approach: You come over the crest and it is below you, roof-first, exactly when you need it.
vibe.senses: Wind that stops abruptly as you drop into the hollow; a horn; a fire.

why.founding: The province has almost no rock, so its caves are root galleries — and the fringe's fig-root mats make the westernmost of them.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the root layer runs over a drained hollow, the roots hold a roof and the ground beneath has gone.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing keeps it; the poachers below use its mouth and will not go past the second chamber.
why.pressures: The roots are alive and moving, on a timescale of years, so the gallery's shape changes.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close on itself in a decade if the figs above it were felled.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the root layer is continuous — galleries connect, and that connection is the map
hardConstraints: a live root roof over a drained void

vibe.silhouette: A dark mouth under a fig root buttress, the roof of the passage entirely made of living wood.
vibe.palette: Root brown, black interior, and green light only at the mouth.
vibe.materials: No masonry anywhere; the architecture is a tree's underside.
vibe.signatureFeature: The floor: bare drained earth under a ceiling that is visibly growing.
vibe.condition: Alive; passages that were open last year are closing.
vibe.approach: You would walk over it without noticing; the mouth is behind a buttress and faces away from the path.
vibe.senses: Roots creaking; dripping; something further in that stops when you stop.

places.name: Keeps-The-Terrace
sources: uesp:Lore:Xanmeer (actively maintained so the mistakes of the past are not repeated)

why.founding: A Merethic xanmeer at the province's western edge, tended by the nearest village as a monument and not as a dungeon.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise above the flood with a terrace that has never been under water — which is why it was built there.
why.occupantsMotive: The village keeps it swept because keeping it swept is what their office is; entering it to loot is a serious offence and they will tell you so.
why.pressures: Gideon's antiquities trade is two days away and getting closer every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be sealed by its own keepers the first time a theft succeeded.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: a landmark for its whole district; a village within 1 km tends it

notableNpcSlots: the terrace-keeper who explains the offence

vibe.silhouette: A stepped pyramid rising clear of the tree canopy, swept, with cut vegetation stacked neatly at its base.
vibe.palette: Pale grey stone, sharp black terrace shadows, green canopy below.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer ashlar, maintained with nothing but brooms and knives; not one stone has been added.
vibe.signatureFeature: The absence of vegetation: the only unvegetated stone surface for kilometres, and it is kept that way by hand.
vibe.condition: Immaculate outside, untouched inside.
vibe.approach: It breaks the canopy — one of the province's two working long-range landmarks, and this is the western one.
vibe.senses: Brooms on stone; wind at terrace height; the canopy below, loud with birds.

why.founding: A province that distrusts metal still needs edges, and this scree has been worked for stone tools since the Merethic.
why.siteAdvantages: A scree of fine-grained stone below a rim cliff — the only workable lithic source in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families come up each dry season and work it, as their families have for longer than anyone counts.
why.pressures: Gideon's iron is cheaper and worse, and the young increasingly buy it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would go quiet within two generations, and the floor would still be here, which is the point.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a village or a hunting ground

vibe.silhouette: A flat apron of grey scree with sitting hollows worn in it and a glitter of flake debris over everything.
vibe.palette: Grey on grey, and a mica glitter that moves as you move.
vibe.materials: No structure at all: a wind-break of stacked stone and thousands of years of flakes.
vibe.signatureFeature: The sitting hollows, worn into the rock by generations of knappers in the same four places.
vibe.condition: Continuously used and entirely unbuilt.
vibe.approach: The glitter is the cue and it only reads with the sun behind you.
vibe.senses: Stone struck on stone, a very particular ringing knock; wind; nothing else.

places.name: Onkobra Divers' Yard

why.founding: The lake has a drowned Kothringi town in it and three centuries of boats on top of that, and Argonians can simply go down and look.
why.siteAdvantages: A shingle beach with deep water twenty metres out — the shortest swim to the good ground on the whole lake.
why.occupantsMotive: The divers work the wrecks and avoid the town, because the town is prohibited and the wrecks are not.
why.pressures: Two of the younger divers have started working the town at night, and the yard is dividing over it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be rich and finished within five years if the prohibition broke.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

notableNpcSlots: the yard elder who forbids the town
the young diver who goes anyway

vibe.silhouette: A shingle beach with a boat rack, a sorting frame of dripping salvage, and a line of drying rope.
vibe.palette: Wet grey shingle, green bronze, rope brown, lake silver.
vibe.materials: Timber racks and frames; every object on them came out of the water.
vibe.signatureFeature: The sorting frame's forbidden shelf, where Kothringi stone-work would go if anyone admitted to bringing it up.
vibe.condition: Working, wet, in permanent slow decay from the water.
vibe.approach: The drying line is visible from the water for a good distance — a horizontal cue in a vertical province.
vibe.senses: Dripping; a bell rung when a diver surfaces late; gulls that are not sea gulls.

places.name: The Lamp at the Ford
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (no long sightlines below the rim)

why.founding: A house at an upland ford that keeps a lamp burning all night, because the ford is unmarked and people drowned before it did.
why.siteAdvantages: The ford is the only crossing for two kilometres and the banks are steep enough to hide it.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper's family took on the lamp as a debt to a drowned cousin and has kept it eighty years.
why.pressures: Lamp oil is expensive here and the family is not rich; guests are expected to understand this.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would go dark the year the family fails, and the ford would start killing again.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: on a route, with a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

occupants: D2 travellers off the upland track

vibe.silhouette: One lit window and a lamp on a pole, at night the only light in a black valley.
vibe.palette: Lamp yellow, wet slate, black water.
vibe.materials: Local stone footings, timber above, a reed roof kept low against the valley wind.
vibe.signatureFeature: The lamp pole, taller than the house, with a counterweight to lower it in wind.
vibe.condition: Small, thickly built, spotless.
vibe.approach: The lamp is the cue and it works only within about six hundred metres — this province's sightlines in one object.
vibe.senses: Water over stones; the pole rope; a kettle.

places.name: Last Post

why.founding: Somebody has to stand where the province ends, and after the Empire left it was the Argonians who kept doing it.
why.siteAdvantages: The narrowest point of the road cut, with rock either side — a gate that needs almost no wall.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers are villagers under a rota, and they check for disease and for slavers, in that order.
why.pressures: Cyrodiil's side is unmanned, which the keepers find both restful and insulting.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a real frontier if anything on the other side ever came back.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: spaced along the border; gaps are the point
preferences: a view down the Cyrodiil side

occupants: one strong D3 in the wet season
notableNpcSlots: the keeper who checks tongues for the Flu that ended two centuries ago

vibe.silhouette: A barrier pole, a bench, a reed hut, and rock walls on both sides of a road that goes on without them.
vibe.palette: Rock grey, unpainted timber, the green of the Cyrodiil side which is visibly different green.
vibe.materials: Timber and reed, on Imperial road stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tongue bench, where every comer sits to be looked at — a Knahaten habit that outlived the disease.
vibe.condition: Minimal, kept, unfortified.
vibe.approach: The cut narrows, and there is a pole across the road, and the light changes because the vegetation changes.
vibe.senses: Wind funnelling; the barrier counterweight; birds that only live on one side.

places.name: Leaning Watch

why.founding: The tower's twin, built on ground that turned out to be a peat lens rather than rock.
why.siteAdvantages: It has the same commanding view and is falling into it at about a degree a decade.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; children dare each other up it and a hermit sleeps in the base in winter.
why.pressures: It leans towards the road, which everyone finds ominous and nobody finds urgent.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would come down entirely in one wet season, and the villages have a wager on the year.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands a route or a channel
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower
preferences: intact stair to the second floor only

occupants: D2 nesting hackwing in the upper floor

vibe.silhouette: A stone tower out of plumb by a clear four degrees, its top course open to the sky.
vibe.palette: Green-black damp on the low side, dry pale grey on the high side.
vibe.materials: Same Imperial rubble as its twin — the identical build failing differently is the point.
vibe.signatureFeature: The lean itself, and the dropped plumb line some surveyor left hanging inside a century ago.
vibe.condition: Dangerous above the second floor and obviously so.
vibe.mood: Absurd, slightly sinister, a good climb.
vibe.approach: Only readable at close range, and then unmistakable.
vibe.senses: Grit falling inside the shaft; birds; the tower creaking in wind, which it should not do.

places.name: Ledge of Tallies
sources: uesp:Lore:Gideon (the Blackwood Road) (the legal crossings are few)

why.founding: There is exactly one legal crossing into Cyrodiil, so every other crossing is on the rim and none of them are level.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench with a ravine below and a saddle above — goods can be lowered to it from one province and lifted to the other.
why.occupantsMotive: The carriers here are village men from both sides who have worked the same ledge for generations.
why.pressures: Fort Swampmoth's company has begun pricing the legal road so high that the ledge is now busier than it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the tolls ever dropped, which would be the cheapest border policy available.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: none; this is the dry route
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: beside a pass, out of sight of its post
hardConstraints: a bench between a ravine and a saddle

notableNpcSlots: the ledge-master who keeps the tally

vibe.silhouette: A ledge with a rope bollard cut into the rock and two hundred tally marks beside it.
vibe.palette: Rock grey, rope brown, deep ravine shadow, one strip of sky.
vibe.materials: Cut bollards, rope, a hide-covered cache — every fixing is in rock because nothing else survives here.
vibe.signatureFeature: The tally wall: a mark per load, generations deep, the oldest ones nearly worn away.
vibe.condition: Maintained where it bears weight, otherwise nothing.
vibe.approach: You do not see it from anywhere; you climb to it, and the tally wall tells you you were expected.
vibe.senses: Rope under load; rock fall; wind in the ravine.

places.name: The Marble Field

why.founding: Imperials buried their dead here for two centuries in a province where burial does not work.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry knoll outside the walls, chosen by people who assumed dry knolls stay dry.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it; the Imperial families left, and Argonians will not tend a grave, having other arrangements.
why.pressures: The water table rose; a third of the plots have surfaced, and the city does not discuss it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be cleared if anyone in Gideon were willing to touch it, which nobody is.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: attached to a foreign settlement
hardConstraints: a knoll outside a city wall

occupants: D1 by day; the province does not raise its dead

vibe.silhouette: A field of pale stelae leaning at every angle, half of them fallen, on a knoll in sight of the city.
vibe.palette: Grey-white marble, green ground, black damp in the lettering.
vibe.materials: Imported Nibenese marble — the only marble in the province and it was spent on the dead.
vibe.signatureFeature: The surfaced plots: rows where the ground has given up its boxes and nobody has put them back.
vibe.condition: Collapsing quietly, unvisited, un-vandalised because the locals will not touch it.
vibe.approach: The white shows through grass from the city road; it is the only white in the landscape.
vibe.senses: Grass; the city faintly; an absence of the birds you would expect.

why.founding: A Maran mission on the Blackwood Road, whose brothers died of swamp rot inside a month — the same fate as Umpholo, on the road instead of the interior.
why.siteAdvantages: Built on what the surveyors called firm ground and the locals called a wet-season island.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the road villages route around it, and the routing is a hundred and eighty years old.
why.pressures: It is being eaten by fig roots at a rate that can be measured year to year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have been a village if it had been sited fifty metres higher — which is the sermon the locals draw from it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: far inland, where nobody wanted them
hardConstraints: off the road on a wet-season island

vibe.silhouette: A stone apse with no nave left, standing in scrub with a fig growing out of the altar.
vibe.palette: Grey stone, fig green, the black of a crypt stair full of water.
vibe.materials: Imperial chapel masonry; the timber went for firewood within a decade.
vibe.signatureFeature: The brothers' names cut into the apse wall by the last of them, in a hand that deteriorates down the list.
vibe.condition: One wall standing, the rest a footprint in the grass, crypt flooded.
vibe.approach: The path bends away from it deliberately; you have to leave the path, which is the whole discovery.
vibe.senses: Water in the crypt; fig leaves; nothing else.

places.name: Niben Crystal Workings

why.founding: Niben-crystal comes out of the Blackwood's hills, and the enchanters' benches of two provinces will buy it.
why.siteAdvantages: A ravine wall where the seam is exposed by the water that cut it — the river did the prospecting.
why.occupantsMotive: A family works the seam and sells to whichever side pays; they have no politics and say so.
why.pressures: The seam runs under the ravine floor, which means working in water, which is killing them slowly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be taken over by an outside concession the day the family failed.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: supplies an artisan village's jewellers
hardConstraints: an exposed seam in a ravine wall

occupants: D3 in the ravine after rain

vibe.silhouette: Timber staging pinned to a ravine wall, with a seam of glassy blue-green running behind it.
vibe.palette: Blue-green crystal, wet black rock, timber that is always dark with water.
vibe.materials: Lashed timber staging and rope ladders; nothing here is founded on the ground.
vibe.signatureFeature: The seam itself, catching the one hour of direct light the ravine gets.
vibe.condition: Rebuilt after every flood, which is annually.
vibe.mood: Precarious, valuable, damp to the bone.
vibe.approach: You hear the water first; the seam glints for about an hour a day and otherwise the place is invisible.
vibe.senses: Hammer taps on rock; water; timber shifting.

places.name: Old Office House

why.founding: Some village offices are held by a household rather than a village, and that household lives apart from both.
why.siteAdvantages: Midway between four villages on the only ground none of them claims.
why.occupantsMotive: The holder settles boundary and water disputes for all four, and lives apart so that she can.
why.pressures: Her heir does not want the office, and no other household will take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would leave four villages arguing directly with each other, which none of them wants.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: 200-600 m from the village it serves

notableNpcSlots: the officeholder
the reluctant heir

vibe.silhouette: One house with four paths converging on it and a long bench outside the door facing the yard.
vibe.palette: Thatch gold, packed-earth yard, four different path colours arriving.
vibe.materials: Ordinary mud and reed, kept plain because plainness is part of the office.
vibe.signatureFeature: The four paths, worn to different depths, which is a record of which village argues most.
vibe.condition: Modest and immaculate.
vibe.approach: The converging paths are visible from any of the four approaches and read as a decision point.
vibe.senses: A slow conversation on the bench; a kettle; nothing hurried.

why.founding: The living quarters of a plantation whose crop failed for good when the drainage silted.
why.siteAdvantages: Built as one long row on the driest line available, which is now the only walkable line through the swamp there.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; people walk through it because the row is the path.
why.pressures: The row is being used as a road by the descendants of the people who were housed in it, without comment.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down for materials if the materials were worth anything.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: near a road that stopped being used
preferences: a collapsed overseer's house at one end

vibe.silhouette: Twenty identical doorways in a row of roofless walls, running dead straight into the trees.
vibe.palette: Grey render, black doorways, green everything else.
vibe.materials: Cheap Imperial brick with reed roofs long gone; the overseer's end was stone.
vibe.signatureFeature: The doorway rhythm: twenty identical openings, and the twenty-first with a lintel and a step.
vibe.condition: Roofless, walls to head height, floors sound enough to walk.
vibe.approach: You are walking a path and the path becomes a corridor of doorways without any transition.
vibe.senses: Your own footsteps between walls; wind through twenty openings at once.

why.founding: Argonians build no prisons, so where the Owing needs to hold someone it uses a pit and calls it waiting.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry storage pit at the back of a broker's yard, roofed and grated, invisible from the road.
why.occupantsMotive: The brokers hold debtors here for a day or two until the Owing is transferred, which is legal and looks like nothing else.
why.pressures: Somebody was held for eleven days last year and the village has not stopped talking about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be filled in the week a court ruled that waiting is imprisonment.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: attached to a hard-owing estate or crossing
preferences: no visible approach from the road

vibe.silhouette: A timber grate flush with a yard floor, with a mat pulled half over it, and nothing else to see.
vibe.palette: Yard dust, dark below the grate, one bright patch of daylight on the pit floor.
vibe.materials: Timber grate, mud-lined pit, a ladder that is kept elsewhere.
vibe.signatureFeature: The ladder's absence — the whole institution is one missing object.
vibe.condition: Serviceable; the mud lining is renewed, which tells you it is used.
vibe.approach: Nothing announces it; you find it because someone in the village makes sure you do.
vibe.senses: Yard noise from above; a voice that is not shouting.

places.name: The Ravine Doors
sources: world/sources/sites/candidate-sites.md (21 gorges, 36 ravines in this zone)

why.founding: Where the rim rivers cut deep, the only flat ground is on the walls, so a community learned to live sideways.
why.siteAdvantages: A gorge wall with a natural bedding plane running along it at two levels — the shelf is the street.
why.occupantsMotive: They live here because the gorge is defensible against everything except the river, and the river is predictable.
why.pressures: The lower shelf floods in a bad year and the upper shelf cannot hold everyone.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move to the rim if the lower shelf were lost, and lose half its people to the lowlands in the process.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: commands a stretch of river; the corridor's signature settlement
hardConstraints: a continuous bedding shelf on a gorge wall

occupants: D3 in the gorge floor after dark
notableNpcSlots: the ladder-keeper

vibe.silhouette: Two lines of doorways in a rock wall, one above the other, with ladders between them and the river far below.
vibe.palette: Rock grey-brown, doorway black, and a strip of bright sky.
vibe.materials: Reed and timber fronts built onto natural rock shelves; almost nothing is freestanding.
vibe.signatureFeature: The ladder system: the village's whole circulation is vertical, and the ladders are pulled up at night.
vibe.condition: Well built, constantly re-lashed, blackened by cooking smoke on the rock above every door.
vibe.approach: From the gorge floor you see cooking smoke coming out of a rock wall, which is the only cue there is.
vibe.senses: Voices from directly above; the river continuously; ladders knocking rock.

places.name: The Ring of Nine Wells

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid ring of well stones, built by the exiles who came east out of Cyrodiil and set their wells where the ground was highest.
why.siteAdvantages: A broad low dome of firm ground with sightlines between all nine positions — the only such ground in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the local villages use the ring as a place to meet and refuse to sleep in it.
why.pressures: Three wells still charge at dusk and six do not, and the Synod would very much like to know why.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a Synod compound the week Gideon's council granted a lease.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in Ayleid country
preferences: at least three intact well stones

occupants: D3 after dark near the live stones

vibe.silhouette: Nine white stumps in a wide circle on open ground, three of them faintly blue at dusk.
vibe.palette: Bone white, dusk blue, dry grass gold.
vibe.materials: Barsaebic Ayleid dressed stone and welkynd fittings; nothing has been added in four thousand years.
vibe.signatureFeature: The three live wells and the six dead ones, indistinguishable until the light goes.
vibe.condition: Weathered to stumps, structurally trivial, magically intact in part.
vibe.mood: Open, ancient, mildly uncanny at exactly one time of day.
vibe.approach: In daylight you can see the whole ring from outside it; at dusk you cannot see anything else.
vibe.senses: A very low hum near the live stones; wind; the grass laid flat in a circle.

places.name: Rests-The-Walkers

why.founding: Nisswo walk, and walking priests need houses at walking intervals along the pilgrim road.
why.siteAdvantages: Half a day from Glenbridge, at the point where the road leaves the firm ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The resident Nisswo hears the road's confessions, which are mostly about money.
why.pressures: The road's Imperial travellers keep mistaking the house for an inn and being fed anyway.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be kept up by the pilgrims themselves if the Nisswo ever left.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: between villages on a preaching circuit
hardConstraints: half a day's walk from the shrine

notableNpcSlots: the road Nisswo

vibe.silhouette: A small house with a black-painted door and a bench outside it facing the road, nothing else.
vibe.palette: Black door, ochre wall, road dust.
vibe.materials: Mud and reed, kept plain deliberately; the only paint in the building is on the door.
vibe.signatureFeature: The bench, worn into two hollows: one for the Nisswo and one for whoever sits down.
vibe.condition: Modest and immaculate.
vibe.approach: It is the only black door on the road and it reads at a hundred metres.
vibe.senses: A kettle; the road; long silences that are not awkward.

why.founding: The Second Empire tried to make the Onkobra navigable to the uplands with a staircase of stone locks.
why.siteAdvantages: At the reach where the river drops fastest — the only place locks would have been needed and the worst place to build them.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; the villages downstream fish the pools the ruined chambers make.
why.pressures: The masonry is a millennium older than the Imperial work below and visibly better, which nobody comments on.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worth rebuilding if anyone wanted freight in the uplands, and nobody does.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: under or beside later Imperial works

vibe.silhouette: Four stone chambers stepping up a wooded gorge, each one now a still green pool with a waterfall into it.
vibe.palette: Deep shade green, wet black stone, white water at each step.
vibe.materials: Second Empire ashlar — huge blocks, tight joints, no mortar visible.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gate recesses, still square, with the pintles still in them and no gates for a thousand years.
vibe.condition: Structurally superb; the ironwork is gone and the chambers are silted to half depth.
vibe.approach: There is no path; you follow the river up and the first chamber is simply there.
vibe.senses: Four waterfalls at different pitches; dripping; echo off dressed stone.

places.name: The Second Hearth

why.founding: Argonians raised outside a Hist's reach have nowhere to go home to; on the Imperial fringe there are more of them than anywhere but the ports.
why.siteAdvantages: Close enough to Gideon for work, far enough that nobody has to explain themselves twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because the settlement is the only place their gloor-faded skin is unremarkable.
why.pressures: The interior villages call them lukiul and mean it; Hissmir's pilgrimage is a two-week walk they cannot all make.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty towards Hissmir if the League ever funded the journey — a live quest lever.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: wherever they were allowed to stop
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the edge of somewhere that would not take them in
preferences: a made hearth-ring at the centre where a Hist would be

notableNpcSlots: the speaker who has never seen a Hist
the child who has

vibe.silhouette: A ring of houses around a bare central circle where the tree should be, with a stone hearth in its place.
vibe.palette: Washed-out ochre, pale scales, and one deliberately empty green-less centre.
vibe.materials: Standard mud-and-wattle round houses, arranged in a grammar that expects a Hist and does not have one.
vibe.signatureFeature: The empty centre: a hearth ring where every other Argonian village has roots.
vibe.condition: Newly built, well built, permanent-looking in a culture that does not build permanent.
vibe.approach: The gap in the middle reads from the approach — you notice the absence before the houses.
vibe.senses: Ordinary village noise, and a silence at the centre of it.

why.founding: Glenbridge cannot house everyone who comes for the sermon, so the overflow camps a mile short and walks in at dawn.
why.siteAdvantages: A flat river meadow with water, firewood and no landlord.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims camp here because arriving at dawn is considered better; the innkeepers price the difference.
why.pressures: Foreign pilgrims and Nisswo pilgrims camp at opposite ends and neither will say why.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a village if the sermon ever drew a permanent crowd, and Glenbridge would fight it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: water and firm ground on a pilgrim route
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the last stop before a sacred destination
hardConstraints: a mile short of a pilgrimage site

vibe.silhouette: Sixty small fires in a meadow at dusk, in two distinct clusters with a clear gap between them.
vibe.palette: Fire orange, meadow grey-green, black Nisswo cloth at one end and every other colour at the other.
vibe.materials: Bedrolls, awnings, a shared water point; the ground is worn bare in the same two patches every year.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gap: forty metres of unused meadow between the two camps, maintained by nobody and by everybody.
vibe.condition: Seasonal; out of season the two bare patches remain.
vibe.mood: Devout, sociable, sectarian in a low-key way.
vibe.approach: The fires are visible from the road at dusk and from nowhere at all in daylight.
vibe.senses: Two different chants at once; kettles; a dawn stir that starts in the dark.

places.name: The Shaking House

why.founding: The marsh gives travellers fevers that villages will not risk, so the sick are put somewhere apart and tended anyway.
why.siteAdvantages: Downwind and downstream of the village, on its own spit, with clean water carried in.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper is a survivor of swamp rot who cannot catch it again and knows it.
why.pressures: The village pays in food and never visits; the keeper's own family have not crossed the spit in nine years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be burned and rebuilt fifty metres along at the first sign of anything the keeper does not recognise.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: 200-600 m outside an M3+ settlement
hardConstraints: downwind and downstream of a settlement

notableNpcSlots: the keeper who cannot catch it again

vibe.silhouette: A long low shed on a spit, a burning ground beside it, and a bell on a post at the water's edge.
vibe.palette: Lime white inside, smoke grey outside, brown water between it and everything else.
vibe.materials: Limewashed wattle, reed roof renewed yearly, a stone burning floor.
vibe.signatureFeature: The bell post on the far bank, with a shelf under it for what the village leaves.
vibe.condition: Scrupulously clean, deliberately cheap to burn.
vibe.approach: You see the bell post first, on your side of the water, and the shed across from it.
vibe.senses: The bell; coughing carried over water; lime and woodsmoke.

places.name: Door-That-Stayed-Shut

why.founding: A xanmeer deliberately closed by its own people, with its traps live and its contents undisturbed.
why.siteAdvantages: Low ground that has since half-drowned, so the sealed door is now at water level and the upper terraces are an island.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it; the nearest village knows it is there and treats knowing as sufficient.
why.pressures: Water is getting in below the seal, which will eventually open it from underneath.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become the west's most dangerous place the day the water finished the job.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: deliberately hard to reach; no village tends it

occupants: D4 mechanisms and what they were set against

vibe.silhouette: An island of stone terraces in shallow water, with a sealed door two hand-widths above the waterline.
vibe.palette: Waterline green-black on grey stone; above the line, dry pale grey.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer ashlar and one vakka-stone seal plate, unbroken.
vibe.signatureFeature: The seal itself — unbroken, and the reason to come, and the reason not to.
vibe.condition: Perfectly preserved above water; being undermined below it.
vibe.approach: The terraces show above the reeds by boat at about two hundred metres; the door does not show at all.
vibe.senses: Water against stone; a hollow note when the seal plate is struck; nothing from inside.

places.name: The Silent Halls

why.founding: A Merethic xanmeer opened long ago and taken over by the Sul-Xan, who use its chambers to keep what their snares catch.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep stone below the water table: cool, dark, and quiet enough that the name is literal.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep it because a soul-store needs walls; nobody contests it because the tribes will not enter a xanmeer that has been broken.
why.pressures: The mechanism floor still works, and the Sul-Xan do not understand it; the Four Winds want the place burned.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a tended xanmeer again if a tribe with a claim ever took it back and closed it.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a district with other xanmeer, showing the range of states
hardConstraints: a lower chamber below water table
preferences: no natural light beyond the first chamber

notableNpcSlots: the warden who counts the gems

vibe.silhouette: A low, mostly buried terrace in the trees with one forced doorway, its lintel cracked and propped.
vibe.palette: Black doorway, pale stone, jade points of light inside.
vibe.materials: Xanmeer ashlar, vakka-stone fittings, Sul-Xan hide and cord strung through it like a nest in a machine.
vibe.signatureFeature: The gem shelf: hundreds of soul-gems in dead men's niches, faintly lit.
vibe.condition: Broken open, occupied, half its mechanisms still armed.
vibe.approach: The forest noise stops about thirty metres out, which is the actual cue.
vibe.senses: No insects; your own footsteps too loud; a faint singing from the gem shelf.

places.name: The Snowline Cell
sources: uesp:Lore:Black Marsh (the province's northern and western rim)

why.founding: Above the marsh's ceiling there is cold, dry air and no disease, and one order of ascetics has decided that is the point.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest saddle on the western rim, where snow lies for a few weeks a year — the only cold ground in Argonia.
why.occupantsMotive: Two ascetics winter here to prove that an Argonian can, which is a theological claim, not a boast.
why.pressures: One of them is dying of the cold and both are treating that as evidence.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be empty in a decade unless the practice attracts a third.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the rim's signature dwelling; deliberately alone
preferences: a fuel store bigger than the cell

notableNpcSlots: the elder ascetic
the one who is dying

vibe.silhouette: A drystone cell the size of a cart, built into a saddle wall, with a fuel stack twice its size beside it.
vibe.palette: Stone grey, snow white for six weeks, brown fuel stack, and below it the entire green province.
vibe.materials: Dry stone and hauled peat. No reed, no mud — the two materials the province is built from are both absent.
vibe.signatureFeature: The fuel stack: everything here is about fuel, and the stack is the largest structure.
vibe.condition: Solid, tiny, immaculately dry inside.
vibe.approach: Five hours of climbing, and then the marsh is a green floor below you — the best view in the province.
vibe.senses: Wind, constantly; peat smoke; teeth chattering, which they find funny.

places.name: The Standing Mist
sources: docs/world/55-light-sky-time.md (mist is a climate field per region class)

why.founding: A cold-air hollow on the rim where the mist forms every night and does not lift until midday.
why.siteAdvantages: A box canyon with a spring in it: cold water, still air, no through-draught.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; two villages graze its edges and neither will take stock into it before noon.
why.pressures: Things are lost in it regularly, including two people in the last decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be ordinary ground if the spring ever failed, and the villages would be sorry.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: visible as a feature from a nearby high point
hardConstraints: a closed hollow with a cold spring
preferences: something worth finding in the middle

occupants: D3 that hunts in the mist

vibe.silhouette: A canyon mouth with a flat white ceiling of mist in it, level as water, that you walk down into.
vibe.palette: White, and then grey, and then whatever is close enough to see.
vibe.materials: Nothing built. There are cairns inside, placed by people trying to find their way out.
vibe.signatureFeature: The mist surface: from above it is a lake of white with the canyon walls standing out of it.
vibe.condition: Unchanged; the cairns accumulate.
vibe.approach: From the rim above you look down on the top of the mist, which is the whole reveal.
vibe.senses: Sound arrives from the wrong direction; dripping; your own voice returning flat.

places.name: Holds-The-Stone
sources: uesp:Lore:Rockgrove (the Ca-Uxith, charged by their Hist to watch the xanmeer; the stone-talkers; the geyser field)

why.founding: The Ca-Uxith were charged by their Hist with watching the Rockgrove xanmeer, and a duty that specific needs a village next to it; the tribe has held this ground for as long as the charge has existed, which is longer than anyone can date.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm shelf before the geyser field, close enough to see the xanmeer's upper courses and far enough that the ground does not vent under the houses.
why.occupantsMotive: The stone-talkers do the actual work — reading the ruin's stone for the cracks the geysers open and packing them before the ruin comes apart. It is preservation as a religious obligation, done with clay and patience.
why.pressures: The Sul-Xan raid camp sits on the ruin the Ca-Uxith are sworn to keep, and the tribe has no means to remove them; the geyser field is getting louder, and the elders disagree about whether that is the ruin's fault or the tribe's.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the xanmeer collapsed, the charge would end and the tribe would have no reason to be here at all — which is a thing several of the young ones have started saying aloud.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: upslope of a geyser field, on spring water that is drinkable and hot
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: within sight of place.imperial-fringe.rockgrove; no other neighbour within an hour
hardConstraints: firm ground clear of the vents
line of sight to the xanmeer
preferences: a stone-talkers' shed of clay, tools and packing rods
drying racks for the packing clay
a Hist at the back of the shelf, not the front

occupants: D3 Sul-Xan raiders working the same ground
notableNpcSlots: the eldest stone-talker, who can hear a crack before it opens
the young one who wants the charge ended

vibe.silhouette: A low village on a shelf with drying racks of grey clay along its edge, and behind it steam standing in columns that do not move with the wind.
vibe.palette: Steam white, packing-clay grey, hot-spring rust-orange on the rock, and a red Hist flower well back from all of it.
vibe.materials: Reed and mud, and a great deal of worked clay — the tribe's craft is packing stone it did not cut and will not quarry.
vibe.signatureFeature: The packing: every visible crack in the xanmeer opposite has a grey clay seam in it, and each seam is dated by a notch, so the ruin wears the tribe's whole record on its face.
vibe.condition: Modest, worn, meticulously maintained in the one respect that matters.
vibe.mood: Dutiful and tired; a village doing a job nobody thanks it for, next to people who are undoing it.
vibe.approach: The steam gives it away long before the roofs do, and the guide who meets you is walking a specific line between vents.
vibe.senses: Vent hiss on a slow rhythm; sulphur under the cooking; the tap of a talker sounding the stone.

provisions: a canon Argonian counterparty to the Sul-Xan at Rockgrove
stone-talkers: a preservation craft the player can be taught or asked to defend
a geyser field as a live, worsening hazard next to a settlement

localStateVariants: charge kept (seams fresh, Sul-Xan at a distance)
charge failing (a new crack unpacked, raiders on the terrace)

places.name: The Sunk Lane

why.founding: The burn country's peat burned out from below in places, and where the roof went the ground simply left.
why.siteAdvantages: One of the province's very few true sinkholes, opened within living memory across an old cart lane.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody uses it; the lane now ends at it, and the ruts run right up to the lip on both sides.
why.pressures: It is still widening, slowly, and the villages measure it with a stake each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would swallow the last of the lane within a generation.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: rare — eleven found province-wide; every instance should be individually meaningful
hardConstraints: an open sinkhole with a rim
preferences: a truncated path on both sides

occupants: D4 in the water at the bottom

vibe.silhouette: A cart lane that stops at a hole thirty metres across with black water at the bottom of it.
vibe.palette: Root-fringed brown walls, black water, the incongruous ordinariness of the cart ruts.
vibe.materials: Nothing built. A line of stakes marks the rim's retreat, one per year.
vibe.signatureFeature: The ruts running to the lip and starting again on the far side.
vibe.condition: Actively enlarging.
vibe.approach: The lane is ordinary until it isn't — the reveal is at ten metres and there is no cue at all.
vibe.senses: Water dripping from roots; a long delay before anything you drop lands.

places.name: The Turned-Out

why.founding: When an Owing is called in against a household's land, the household is not imprisoned — it is simply outside.
why.siteAdvantages: On the verge of the road within sight of the fields they worked, because that is where the brokers put them out.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay in sight deliberately: leaving would be taken as abandoning the claim.
why.pressures: It is the third winter; two families have gone to Gideon and not come back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end tomorrow if the estate voided one ledger — which is precisely why it does not.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: immediately outside an estate village
hardConstraints: on a public verge in sight of the lost holding

occupants: no guards, which is the point
notableNpcSlots: the eldest, who will not move the camp

vibe.silhouette: Six lean-tos of salvaged thatch on a road verge, all facing the same way, at the field they used to work.
vibe.palette: Dust, salvaged straw, and the too-neat green of the fields behind them.
vibe.materials: Salvaged house materials reassembled badly — the thatch is better than the frames because they carried the thatch.
vibe.signatureFeature: The orientation: every shelter faces the fields. Nobody sleeps facing the road.
vibe.condition: Deteriorating, third year, no longer temporary.
vibe.approach: The camp is on the road; you cannot pass it without being seen not stopping.
vibe.senses: Very little noise; a hand mill; children being kept quiet.

places.name: The Two Lamps

why.founding: A hermit who wanted to be unreachable and then, having achieved it, hung a lamp out for anyone who tried.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench forty metres up a ravine wall, reachable by one climb and no path.
why.occupantsMotive: He is here to be alone; the second lamp is for a person he expects and who has not come.
why.pressures: He is old, the climb is not getting easier, and the villages below have begun to worry aloud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a shrine within a year of his death, which he knows and dislikes.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design
hardConstraints: a bench reachable only by climbing
preferences: a lamp bracket visible from below

notableNpcSlots: the hermit with two lamps

vibe.silhouette: A hut wedged on a ledge with two lamps hung from a pole, one lit and one not.
vibe.palette: Rock grey, lamp yellow, the black of the ravine below.
vibe.materials: Stone and driftwood carried up over years; the roof is a single sheet of somebody's boat.
vibe.signatureFeature: The unlit second lamp, cleaned and filled, waiting.
vibe.condition: Improbably sound; every fixing is over-engineered because nothing can be replaced.
vibe.approach: One lamp, forty metres up a black wall — the province's cue language at its purest.
vibe.senses: Wind past the ledge; water dripping; a very quiet voice.

places.name: Vellum Estate

why.founding: An Archein-era estate that survived the end of slavery by converting its slaves into Owing debtors on paper.
why.siteAdvantages: Good drained land on the river terrace, held in one block because it was never divided.
why.occupantsMotive: The estate house holds the ledgers, and the ledgers are the only reason anyone still works the land.
why.pressures: The Chainbreakers know the estate exists; so does the courthouse; the ledgers are technically lawful.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would dissolve overnight if a court ever voided inherited Owings — which is a quest, not a rumour.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: controls a crossing or a landing
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: holds the crossing its neighbours must use
hardConstraints: one undivided block of good land
an estate house with a strong room

notableNpcSlots: the steward who inherited the ledgers
the worker whose grandmother's entry is still open

vibe.silhouette: A pale estate house at the head of an avenue, with two long worker rows at right angles behind it.
vibe.palette: Bleached lime, avenue shade, the dun of the worker rows.
vibe.materials: Imperial estate masonry in front; mud and reed behind; the change happens at one line you can stand on.
vibe.signatureFeature: The strong room window, the only barred opening on the estate, at ledger height.
vibe.condition: Well kept where it is seen from the avenue; the rows are patched by their occupants.
vibe.mood: Polite, immovable, rotten at the root.
vibe.approach: The avenue frames the house from four hundred metres, which is the only deliberate vista in the zone.
vibe.senses: Cicadas; a bell for shift change; no children's voices near the house.

places.name: The White Throat
sources: docs/world/00-core.md (large logical surfaces climbable by default)

why.founding: Where a rim river drops twenty metres it has cut back into the rock and left a room behind the water.
why.siteAdvantages: The undercut is deep enough to stand in and dry enough to keep things in.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; smugglers and one hermit have both used it and left different rubbish.
why.pressures: The fall's flow doubles after rain and the chamber floods to knee height.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a shrine in a province with fewer waterfalls; here it is simply a good room.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on a river with real relief — the rim and upland only
preferences: a dry ledge above flood height
a way in from one side only

occupants: D3 whatever nests behind the water

vibe.silhouette: A curtain of white water with a black slot behind it, invisible until you are level with it.
vibe.palette: White water, black wet rock, green light coming through the fall.
vibe.materials: Nothing built but a stacked stone shelf someone made above flood height.
vibe.signatureFeature: The light: everything inside is lit green through moving water.
vibe.condition: Scoured clean annually; whatever is left has been left recently.
vibe.approach: The fall is audible for four hundred metres and the chamber is invisible until the last three.
vibe.senses: Water at a volume that removes speech; dripping; your own breathing amplified.

why.founding: Where an antiquities market exists, people will camp above the graves that supply it.
why.siteAdvantages: Just over the ridge from the cairn field, out of sight of the valley track and upwind of the smell of their own camp.
why.occupantsMotive: They are here for glass beads, which are small, light, and worth a season's wages in Leyawiin.
why.pressures: The Collections dig pays better and asks questions; two of this camp have already crossed over.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move to the next dead people the month the beads ran out.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: beside a notable ruin or hard-to-reach landform
hardConstraints: out of sight of a route
within an hour of a robbable site

vibe.silhouette: Four hide tents behind a ridge, a sorting mat, and a great deal of broken stone nobody wanted.
vibe.palette: Hide brown, bead blue-green, ridge grey.
vibe.materials: Hide, poles and one stolen conservation tarpaulin they have not bothered to hide.
vibe.signatureFeature: The sorting mat: beads by colour, and a pile of bone pushed aside with a boot.
vibe.condition: Filthy, temporary, well armed.
vibe.approach: Smoke over a ridge from the cairn field, which is how the villages find them too.
vibe.senses: Stone being knapped open; low voices; flies.

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid compound from the exile centuries, close enough to Gideon that the city's antiquities trade starts here.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry terrace over a spring — Ayleid siting logic, and the reason Gideon's diggers keep coming back.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers want stones with light in them; the Collections chapter wants the same stones back; both are here most months.
why.pressures: Every season of digging takes more of the wall; the Barsaebic layer is being consumed to prove it existed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be protected properly if Gideon's council ever thought a ruin was worth a guard.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in the north and west, where the Barsaebic Ayleids went

vibe.silhouette: A white arcade fragment on a green terrace, too geometric to be anything but Ayleid.
vibe.palette: Bone white, moss, and the cold blue of a live well stone.
vibe.materials: Barsaebic Ayleid masonry and welkynd fittings; canvas and rope where the diggers work.
vibe.signatureFeature: The grid: string lines and numbered pegs laid over a floor that already had a grid.
vibe.condition: Half-excavated, weather-damaged where excavation exposed it.
vibe.approach: The white shows through the trees from the Gideon track a good way off — one of the few real sightlines in the province.
vibe.senses: Trowels; a well's cold air; canvas snapping.

why.founding: The correction to the embankment: a line of stone culverts cut and dressed on site, then never laid.
why.siteAdvantages: The stone was dressed where it was quarried, next to the line it was meant to serve.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; squatters took the dressed blocks for foundations until the tribes made stone-taking a quarrel.
why.pressures: Post-Duskfall, building in dead stone is a moral error here, so the blocks sit where they were left.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would vanish in a decade if anyone with a use for stone lived nearby.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: on the line of an abandoned Imperial road
hardConstraints: a line of dressed but unlaid stone
preferences: a quarry scrape at one end

vibe.silhouette: Sixty dressed stone rings lying in a line in long grass, like a sentence nobody finished.
vibe.palette: Pale dressed stone against unmown green; lichen only on the top faces.
vibe.materials: Cut Imperial voussoirs and ring segments, tooling marks still crisp.
vibe.signatureFeature: The numbers: every block is chiselled with its position, and the positions run out at forty-one.
vibe.condition: Untouched, unweathered underneath, sinking slowly.
vibe.approach: You walk into it before you see it — the grass is as tall as the rings.
vibe.senses: Nothing; a startling amount of nothing.

places.name: Weighed Cart

why.founding: Gideon's council put a tower where the road forks for the clay pits, because the pits' output is the one export it can measure.
