why.siteAdvantages: A knoll commanding both forks and the river landing below them.
why.occupantsMotive: The tower's clerk is paid on what he records, so he records everything.
why.pressures: The potters route half their carts round it by night and everyone knows.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pointless if the clay bank moved, which it does every generation.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: commands a channel or a road
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one of a chain; must see a neighbour or it is not a watch
hardConstraints: a rise with a view of both branches

occupants: D1 tower clerk and two guards

vibe.silhouette: A squat two-storey stone tower with an external stair and a weigh beam jutting from the first floor.
vibe.palette: Soot-grey stone, red clay dust on everything below waist height.
vibe.materials: Imperial rubble masonry, a reed-roofed lean-to, one iron beam that is the most valuable object for a kilometre.
vibe.signatureFeature: The seizure shelf: unclaimed pots, going back decades, on a shelf under the stair.
vibe.condition: Serviceable, grubby, over-stocked with confiscations.
vibe.approach: Visible from the clay pits and from the fork; the beam sticks out like a gibbet.
vibe.senses: The beam creaking; a tally being called; carts changing gear on the slope.

places.name: Westfield

why.founding: Argonian villagers took up field agriculture from their Imperial neighbours and now grow it better than they do.
why.siteAdvantages: Temperate grassland on the saddle's western apron: the only large stretch of arable in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm because grain sells in Gideon at whatever price they ask in a bad year.
why.pressures: The fields are held in common and the Imperial grants overlap them on paper; nobody has tested it in court.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fight, in court or otherwise, the first time somebody did.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: in a city's agricultural hinterland

notableNpcSlots: the field-holder who keeps the common register

vibe.silhouette: Round mud houses with conical thatch sitting in the middle of open grain fields — two grammars in one view.
vibe.palette: Grain gold, thatch gold, mud-wall ochre, the dark green of the field-edge trees.
vibe.materials: Argonian mud-and-wattle round houses; a stilted granary; not one straight boundary anywhere.
vibe.signatureFeature: The threshing floor: a beaten clay disc bigger than any house in the village.
vibe.condition: Thriving, expanding, rebuilt on a rolling cycle so a quarter of it is always new.
vibe.mood: Confident, communal, quietly competitive with the Imperials next door.
vibe.approach: The fields start abruptly and the roofs are lower than the standing grain until you are close.
vibe.senses: Threshing; a work song; grain dust in the light.

places.name: Low Fen House

why.founding: The College of Whispers works where nobody watches, and the fen edge is the least watched habitable ground near Gideon.
why.siteAdvantages: A stilt house over standing water, reachable by one pole-punt and no path at all.
why.occupantsMotive: They study Hist-sap chemistry and say they study hydrology.
why.pressures: The village that ferries them has begun to ask what the barrels are for.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be gone overnight, house and all, if the question were ever pressed properly.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: a quiet way out by water
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: inside a settlement, indistinguishable from it
preferences: a barrel store below the floor

occupants: one D3 who is not a scholar
notableNpcSlots: the scholar with the barrels

vibe.silhouette: An ordinary reed stilt house with too many shutters, alone on open water, no path to it.
vibe.palette: Reed grey-gold, black water, one green-glass window that is not local glass.
vibe.materials: Local stilt construction, deliberately — the disguise is the architecture.
vibe.signatureFeature: The under-floor store: barrels slung below the platform, in the water, out of sight.
vibe.condition: Unremarkable on purpose; excellent underneath.
vibe.approach: You are punted to it and it looks like every other stilt house until you are under the floor.
vibe.senses: Water under boards; something being decanted; unusual silence for a fen.

why.founding: The ground where a whole community was killed in 1E 2820, and where the Sul-Xan trace their grievance from. Lore:Xi-Tsei puts the site on the southern strip of Blackwood, which is administered as Cyrodiil; we place it inside our province deliberately, because the border there has moved more than once and the massacre is Argonian history wherever the line currently runs.
why.siteAdvantages: An open flat between two ridges — the only place in the Blackwood where an army could be made to stand and fight.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the Sul-Xan come annually and leave marks; the Four Winds come annually and remove them.
why.pressures: Two peoples curate the same field in opposite directions, and both editions are visible.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be settled again only if both traditions lapsed, which neither will.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: where an army could deploy — rare here
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: at a xanmeer, a crossing or a road
hardConstraints: an open flat with two ridge flanks

vibe.silhouette: A wide empty flat with grass growing in rows nobody planted, and a single pole at the centre.
vibe.palette: Straw-gold grass, rust in the soil, grey ridges either side.
vibe.materials: No architecture at all: bone, corroded iron, jade chips, and a pole that is replaced yearly.
vibe.signatureFeature: The counter-marks: painted jade tallies, and beside each one a scrubbed patch where it was removed.
vibe.condition: Undisturbed except by two rituals.
vibe.approach: The ridges close in and the ground goes level and treeless — you know before you are told.
vibe.senses: Wind only; the pole's cords; no birds on the flat itself.
